items.title: 英米の銀行、ＥＵの新規制下でも域内向け融資を継続へ　「逆勧誘」の例外活用
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Phoebe Seers

[ロンドン １２日 ロイター] - 英国と米国の一部銀行は、欧州連合（ＥＵ）の新たな越境取引...
items.body:
英米の銀行、ＥＵの新規制下でも域内向け融資を継続へ　「逆勧誘」の例外活用
11:14 配信

欧州員会の本部。４月２９日、ベルギーのブリュッセルで撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Yves Herman）（ロイター） Phoebe Seers

[ロンドン １２日 ロイター] - 英国と米国の一部銀行は、欧州連合（ＥＵ）の新たな越境取引規制の例外規定を利用し、来年もＥＵ域内向けの融資を続ける方針であることが分かった。ＥＵが域内で監督下にある金融機関を通じた取引を増やそうとしていることが背景にある。事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

弁護士３人と業界関係者２人が語ったところによると、英米の銀行は「逆勧誘（リバース・ソリシテーション）」と呼ばれる例外規定を利用し、本国からの融資を継続しようとしている。この規定は、ＥＵ域内の顧客が自らの意思で銀行に接触した場合に融資を認めるものだ。

ＥＵは来年１月から、ＥＵ域外に本拠を置く銀行について、認可を受けた支店または子会社を通じない限り、域内への多くの金融サービスの直接提供を禁止する。この規制は今年７月以降に契約された融資に適用される。

欧州委員会の報道官は、海外銀行によるこの例外規定の利用をどの程度見込んでいるかとの質問に対し、通常はＥＵ企業が海外に投資する際に使われるものだと説明した。

複数の関係者によると、逆勧誘の例外規定をどこまで広く適用できるのか、また監督当局が長期にわたる広範な利用を認めるのかは不透明だ。銀行各社は、例外規定の適用方法を巡り、当局側と協議を進めているという。

ルクセンブルク金融監督委員会（ＣＳＳＦ）で銀行監督部門を率いるクロード・ワンパック氏は、逆勧誘の適用範囲は限定的で、従来通りの事業を続けるための「特効薬」にはならないとの見解を示した。同国では銀行の約１０％をＥＵ域外勢が占めている。

items.body:
ＡＩチップ供給網、27年を通じて逼迫続く＝中国ＳＭＩＣ
11:13 配信

中芯国際集成電路製造（ＳＭＩＣ）のロゴ。２０２０年１０月、中国・上海で撮影。REUTERS/Aly Song（ロイター） Che Pan　Eduardo Baptista

[北京 １３日 ロイター] - 中国最大の半導体受託製造会社である中芯国際集成電路製造（ＳＭＩＣ）は１３日、人工知能（ＡＩ）業界は依然として初期段階にあり、需要は堅調に推移していると述べた。

この見解はＡＩ関連株にバブルが形成されつつあるかどうかという質問に対する回答としてなされた。

• ＳＭＩＣは「コンピューティングリソースを必要とする多くの顧客は依然として不足に直面」と分析。

• データセンターやプライベートクラウドからの需要により、ＡＩ関連アプリケーション向けの半導体サプライチェーン（供給網）は２０２７年を通じて逼迫した状態が続くと指摘。

• 半導体メモリーの需給は２８年の中盤から後半にかけて均衡に達すると予測。

• ＳＭＩＣは、稼働率が上昇し続けていることから、通年の売上高が１２億ドルを超えると見込んでいる。

Striped socks keep FamilyMart a step ahead in Japan's convenience store wars

FamilyMart has sold 40 million pairs of its striped socks since 2021, turning an unlikely convenience-store hit into a growing fashion business.

A staff member of FamilyMart, known as "Famima", restocks a sock display in the apparel section at the chain’s flagship store in Tokyo, Japan Nov 10, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Issei Kato)

FAST

TOKYO: For some people, the blue, green and white striped socks hanging near the entrance of a FamilyMart convenience store may look more like an emergency purchase than a fashion statement.
Yet the 390 yen (US$2.44) socks have become one of Japan's best-known products at convenience stores, which are usually the go-to for snacks and drinks. With 40 million pairs sold since 2021, they have helped FamilyMart reinvent itself as a lifestyle brand in the competitive "conbini" market.
Now, Japan's second-largest convenience store chain is building on that fashion credential with a wider range of lifestyle items, including matching bandanas for pets and owners, in a push for growth beyond daily necessities. It has also backed the strategy with branding initiatives including a recruitment campaign featuring pop star Lady Gaga.
The effort to cultivate a fashionable image is helping FamilyMart stand out as inflation-weary shoppers cut back on spending, drugstores eat into sales of household staples, and a shrinking population limits expansion opportunities in a market saturated with around 56,000 stores.

"FamilyMart has really upped its style game over the past year or two," said Tatsuhiko Yuki, a 56-year-old taxi driver and regular customer.
Yuki describes FamilyMart as a destination for collectibles, having purchased 20 pairs of its striped socks, including limited-edition versions inspired by Nintendo game "Animal Crossing", along with a dozen other FamilyMart items such as towels.
"Their designs have a retro feel that's just right," he said.
FamilyMart, known as "Famima" and for its blue, white and green branding, launched its Convenience Wear line in 2021, tapping parent Itochu's textile expertise and teaming up with Facetasm streetwear designer Hiromichi Ochiai.
Fuelled by social media buzz, the business has become a more than 20 billion yen operation, with sales set to rise another 30 per cent this fiscal year ending March.
While apparel accounts for less than 1 per cent of FamilyMart's sales and a fraction of Itochu's 2.65 trillion yen in annual gross trading profit, analysts said Convenience Wear helps the chain burnish its image and increase spending by customers visiting its 16,500 stores.
"We've taken a fairly adventurous approach with Convenience Wear," said lineup head Takehiko Sugai at FamilyMart's new flagship Tokyo store, whose creative direction was overseen by Nigo, founder of streetwear label A Bathing Ape.

Tatsuhiko Yuki, wearing FamilyMart's striped socks, attends an interview with Reuters in front of a FamilyMart store in Tokyo, Japan, Oct 16, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Kim Kyung-Hoon)

EDGE BEYOND ESSENTIALS Sugai said FamilyMart combines daily essentials with niche limited-edition collaborations such as Netflix's Stranger Things and the manga series JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, helping draw customers into its stores.
The business will add a pet range in February, which will include collars and leads that allow owners and pets to coordinate outfits.
"Exclusivity is our crucial differentiator from rival chains," Sugai said. "If customers want our products, they have to come to our stores".
FamilyMart declined to disclose how much Convenience Wear is boosting overall store traffic, but Sugai said limited-edition releases regularly generate spikes in customer visits.
Rival Lawson, jointly owned by Mitsubishi Corp and KDDI, has partnered with Ryohin Keikaku to sell Muji-branded products, while Seven-Eleven operator Seven & i Holdings in September expanded its fashion range through collaborations with brands targeting young generations.
But analysts said no rival has matched the cultural resonance of Convenience Wear.
"Famima should be able to keep a degree of competitive edge for a while because they've succeeded in building a loyal customers base that will choose Famima when given a choice of stores," said Hyakunen Consulting economist Takahiro Suzuki.
Declining foot traffic, driven in part by widening income disparities and consumer belt-tightening, means convenience-store operators must seek ways to boost spending per customer while also building a loyal customer base, Suzuki said.
FamilyMart's strategy is not without risk. Fashion trends can be fleeting, and products aimed at younger consumers may struggle to gain traction with the company's broader customer base. Yet Sugai said the sustained popularity of its striped socks suggests Convenience Wear is moving beyond novelty status.
For customers such as Yuki, that approach appears to be working.
"I stop by just to see what's new," he said. "It has become more than a convenience store".

File photo. "Famima" branded food items at the FamilyMart convenience store chain's flagship store, in Tokyo, Japan Nov 10, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Issei Kato)

items.author: ロイター

items.body:
エヌビディア前ＣＥＯと商務長官の議会証言要請＝上院委員長
11:09 配信

写真は５月、エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアン氏。米カリフォルニア州ビバリーヒルズで撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake（ロイター） David Shepardson

[ワシントン １２日 ロイター] - 米議会上院銀行委員会のティム・スコット委員長は１２日、米半導体大手エヌビディアの最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）を辞任したフアン氏とラトニック商務長官に対し、同社の最近の動向について同委員会で証言するよう求める書簡を送付した。

フアン氏は、中国のスパイだったとされる中国人実業家女性と不倫関係にあるとの報道を受けて辞任した。

これを機に、米政府が中国企業数十社を貿易ブラックリストに追加することを拒否した点や、エヌビディアの対中輸出を適切に監督していたかを巡り、議会ではラトニック氏への批判が高まっている。

スコット氏は短文投稿サイト「Ｘ」に「最近の報道により、わが国の国家安全保障と米国の重要技術の保護に関する深刻な懸念が生じた」と投稿し、フアン、ラトニック両氏に証言を求めたと明かした。フアン氏が自発的に応じない場合は召喚状の発行を検討するとしている。

一方、関係者２人によると、ホワイトハウス高官らはラトニック氏を更迭すべきかどうかを協議している。

また下院外交委員会のブライアン・マスト委員長は１２日に記者団に対し、議会スタッフが１１日夜にエヌビディア側と連絡を取り、フアン氏が議員らとの非公開説明会に出席する日程と場所について話し合ったことを明らかにした。

Nov 13 : Hong Kong property developer New World Development has appointed banks to prepare for a rights issue that could raise as much as HK$25 billion ($3.2 billion), Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. 
Trading in New World's shares was halted on Friday pending the release of inside information by the company, according to a pre-market filing to the Hong Kong exchange.
New World did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Hong Kong property developer, the most heavily indebted among its local peers, has been trying to cut debt, dispose of assets and bolster liquidity amid tight credit conditions and a weak property market.

FAST

TOKYO, Nov 13 : The yen could retest 40-year lows against the dollar if the greenback's broad strength and signs of limited US support for Japan's recent currency intervention undermine the threat of further coordinated action, market players said.
The yen weakened past 160 per dollar overnight for the first time since early September, prompting renewed warnings from Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama that Tokyo stood ready to act again after record intervention in July and August.
Japan spent 15.4 trillion yen ($96.5 billion) to bolster its currency after it sank to a four-decade low of 163.99 per dollar in late July. But what gave the operation an extra boost was joint action by the United States, which Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had hinted at the time could reach $10 billion.
A report on Thursday from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, however, showed the total was far lower, amounting to about $497 million of euro sales to buy yen. Analysts say the relatively modest contribution weakens the deterrent effect of any future joint action, even as it confirms Washington was willing to back Tokyo at a critical moment.

"There have been several cases of coordinated intervention, but always the US didn't spend so much money," said Tohru Sasaki, chief strategist at Fukuoka Financial Group and a former Bank of Japan official. "People have been worried that coordinated intervention could be very powerful, but this shows that it's not."
TRADERS MORE WILLING TO TEST SUPPORT
The yen's persistent weakness has become a political and economic headache for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration, lifting the cost of imported fuel and other commodities and squeezing households already struggling with higher prices. It has also added to pressure on the Bank of Japan to continue tightening policy and narrow the interest-rate gap with other major central banks.
Katayama's remarks followed a similar warning on Thursday from top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura, who said it was "too early to forget" this summer's intervention. They also came as markets increasingly expect the Bank of Japan to raise rates next month, with policymakers sounding more alarmed about inflation and the cost of imports caused by the yen's weakness.
But those domestic pressures have in recent days been swamped by a broader dollar rally. The greenback climbed to a 19-month high against major peers as US Treasury yields rose on increased bets on a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike next month.
"Treasury yields right now are seen as a major reason the yen is being sold," said Bart Wakabayashi, branch manager at State Street in Tokyo. "All these comments coming out of the Fed are all indicating higher rates, and I don't think the BOJ is willing to keep up."
That may leave traders more willing to test higher levels, particularly if they conclude that Tokyo acting alone would have only a limited impact and that Washington is reluctant to do much more than lend verbal support.
The New York Fed's currency action "was small as expected, and shows little seriousness on the part of the US in flipping the yen," said Shuhei Uehara, a foreign exchange analyst at Gaitame.com Research Institute.
Chart signals suggest that if dollar/yen pushes through Thursday's peak of 160.30, the next milestone would be 160.39, its high from early September, and that a break above there could open the way toward 164, Uehara said.
Even so, analysts said the diminished threat of joint intervention was unlikely to give speculators a free pass. The 160 line remains a sensitive threshold for Tokyo, and the risk of official action would likely rise if the currency nears this summer's lows.
"The 160-yen level is a closely watched line," said Akira Moroga, chief market strategist at Aozora Bank. "Going forward, they can still intervene on a large scale if they choose. Even if the US doesn't step in, Japan likely will."

Source: Reuters

items.body:
米民主党議員、エヌビディアが「大きすぎてつぶせない」企業か評価要求
10:44 配信

米エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者。２０２５年１２月、ワシントンで撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Evelyn Hockstein）（ロイター） David Shepardson

[ワシントン １２日 ロイター] - 米上院軍事委員会の民主党筆頭委員であるジャック・リード上院議員（ロードアイランド州選出）は１２日、半導体大手エヌビディアが「大きすぎてつぶせない（too big to fail）」企業かどうか、また同社が破綻した場合に米国の銀行・信用市場にどのような影響が及ぶかについて、議会が検討すべきだと述べた。

同社について「複雑な金融取引を通じてＡＩ（人工知能）エコシステムを支えてきた。われわれはこれらの取引に関する完全な透明性の確保、同社が『大きすぎてつぶせない』企業であるかどうかの評価、そしてこうした事態が米国の銀行システムや信用市場にどのような影響を与えるかについての分析を必要としている」と述べた。

エヌビディアは１２日、ジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が辞任すると発表。フアン氏を巡っては、中国のスパイとみられている女性や、社内幹部との不倫行為が取り沙汰されていた。

リード氏は「何百万人もの米国人も、退職金口座や年金基金を通じて、エヌビディアに対する経済的エクスポージャーを抱えている」と述べた。

FAST

HONG KONG, Nov 13 : Chinese AI satellite maker Adaspace Technology slid 1.2 per cent in its Hong Kong market debut on Friday after raising HK$750 million ($95.6 million) in an initial public offering.
• Adaspace opened at HK$24.44, down 1.8 per cent from its HK$24.90 offer price, and last traded at HK$24.60. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 0.5 per cent
• The Chengdu-based company sold 30.12 million shares at the bottom of its HK$24.90 to HK$33.20 marketed range. The retail tranche was 3.43 times subscribed and the international offering was 1.79 times covered
• Adaspace makes AI-powered satellites and provides satellite data services. It plans to use the IPO proceeds for research, satellite production and a Shenzhen research centre
($1 = 7.8441 Hong Kong dollars)

Source: Reuters

items.title: Inside Jensen Huang's Final Hours as the CEO of Nvidia
items.author: Drake Bennett and Ian King
items.creator: Drake Bennett and Ian King
items.summary: At the end, Jensen Huang looked broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted. After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer, his surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. Huang’s usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he’d started using phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”

items.title: Acuerdo de Acciona con MIP por US$1.000 millones está en riesgo de fracasar
items.author: Rodrigo Orihuela, Michael O'Boyle
items.summary: Acciona Energía confirmó que la operación con MIP se retrasó porque no se han cumplido las condiciones de cierre.
items.body: Bloomberg — El acuerdo de Acciona Energía, por valor de US$1.000 millones, para vender activos solares y eólicos a Mexico Infrastructure Partners (MIP) está sufriendo retrasos y corre el riesgo de fracasar, según una persona con conocimiento del asunto. Esto se produce mientras ambas empresas se esfuerzan por ultimar su acuerdo, y Acciona Energía podría ofrecer información actualizada sobre la situación este jueves, según ha indicado dicha persona, que ha solicitado mantener el anonimato, ya que el asunto no es de dominio público. Acciona Energía tiene previsto publicar un comunicado sobre la evolución de sus operaciones a lo largo del día. Aún no se ha tomado ninguna decisión y la operación podría seguir adelante según lo previsto. Ver más: FMI ratifica Línea de Crédito Flexible a México con reducción en monto de financiamiento En un informe de resultados publicado el jueves, Acciona Energía confirmó que la operación con MIP se había retrasado porque no se habían cumplido las condiciones de cierre . El retraso implica que es probable que la empresa no alcance su objetivo de vender activos por valor de unos $2.000 millones de euros (US$2.210 millones), según el comunicado. Un portavoz de MIP se negó a hacer comentarios. Acciona Energía anunció en diciembre de 2025 la operación de venta de cuatro carteras de energía solar en EE.UU. y dos parques eólicos mexicanos a MIP, como parte del programa de rotación de activos de la empresa española de energía limpia. En un principio, estaba previsto que la transacción se cerrara en el primer semestre de 2026. Según los términos del acuerdo, MIP adquiriría una participación del 49% en la cartera estadounidense de 1,3 gigavatios, así como la propiedad íntegra de los dos parques eólicos mexicanos. El vendedor conservará el 51% de los activos estadounidenses y se encargará de su gestión. Acciona Energía, que cotiza en la Bolsa de Madrid, recibe oficialmente el nombre de Corporación Acciona Energías Renovables, S.A. Su accionista mayoritario es Acciona, S.A., que también cotiza en España. (Actualización con la confirmación en el comunicado de resultados, en el cuarto párrafo) Lee más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: "Zero tolerance against terrorism": HM Amit Shah hails extension of ban on Zakir Naik led IRF
items.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on Friday extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), led by fugitive preacher Dr Zakir Naik, declaring the organisation an unlawful association for ...
items.body:
"Zero tolerance against terrorism": HM Amit Shah hails extension of ban on Zakir Naik led IRF The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on Friday extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), led by fugitive preacher Dr Zakir Naik, declaring the organisation an unlawful association for another five years under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), citing its alleged involvement in activities prejudicial to the country's security, communal harmony and secular fabric.
ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 13:43 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 13:43 IST

Fugitive preacher and IRF head Zakri Naik (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on Friday extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), led by fugitive preacher Dr Zakir Naik, declaring the organisation an unlawful association for another five years under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), citing its alleged involvement in activities prejudicial to the country's security, communal harmony and secular fabric. In a post on X, the Office of the Home Minister Amit Shah said,"In steadfast adherence to PM Shri @narendramodi ji's vision of zero tolerance towards terrorism and anti-national activities, MHA extends the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation as an unlawful association under the UAPA. Led by fugitive terror preacher Dr Zakir Naik, the organisation has been involved in sinister anti-India designs, including inciting communal hatred and promoting terrorism. The group has been found to be propagating a venomous ideology of terrorism and separatism, instigating violent unrest, encouraging the regrouping of absconding terrorists and fomenting communal discord."
According to a notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the IRF had been indulging in activities prejudicial to the security of the country, with the potential to disturb peace and communal harmony and disrupt the secular fabric of the country. The notification stated that the Central Government had earlier declared the IRF an unlawful association under Section 3(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, through notifications dated November 17, 2016, and November 15, 2021.
The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal, constituted under Section 5 of the Act to adjudicate whether sufficient grounds existed for declaring the organisation unlawful, had subsequently confirmed the declarations through orders published on May 22, 2017, and March 30, 2022. The notification further noted that the existing ban under Section 6(1) of the Act was due to cease on November 14, 2026.
The Central Government stated that the IRF and its members, particularly its founder and president, Dr Zakir Abdul Karim Naik alias Dr Zakir Naik, had been encouraging and aiding followers to promote or attempt to promote, on religious grounds, disharmony and feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious communities and groups, in a manner prejudicial to the country's integrity and security. The government cited several grounds for its decision, including statements and speeches made by Naik, which it described as "objectionable and subversive".
It further alleged that through these speeches and statements, Naik had been promoting enmity and hatred among different religious groups and inspiring youths belonging to a particular religion in India and abroad to commit terrorist acts. The notification also stated that Naik had made radical statements and speeches to millions of people worldwide through international satellite television networks, the internet, print and social media.
The Central Government expressed apprehension that if the unlawful activities of the IRF were not curbed and controlled immediately, the organisation could continue its subversive activities and reorganise activists who were still absconding. It further stated that the organisation could disrupt the secular fabric of the country by creating communal disharmony, propagate anti-national sentiments, escalate secessionism by supporting militancy and undertake activities prejudicial to the sovereignty, integrity and security of the country.
Invoking Sections 3(1) and 3(3) of the UAPA, 1967, the Central Government declared the Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association with immediate effect. The notification stated that the declaration would remain in force for a period of five years from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette, subject to any order that may be passed under Section 4 of the Act. (ANI)

Samsung is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US-listed maker of cooling systems for data centres, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday (Nov 12), citing people familiar with the matter. 
The companies are discussing a potential deal that could come together as soon as the coming weeks, the report added.
Shares of Modine surged 29 per cent in extended trading following the report. The company had a market value of US$5.6 billion as of Thursday, according to data compiled by LSEG.
No final decision has been made and the talks could still fall apart, the report said, adding that another suitor could also emerge.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Samsung and Modine could not be reached for comment immediately.

Putin lets Europe join Ukraine peace talks, Zelenskiy welcomes prospect of European participation

By Andrew Osborn and Padraic Halpin
MOSCOW/DUBLIN, Nov 12 (Reuters) – President Vladimir Putin agreed on Thursday to let European representatives join the next round of Ukraine peace talks, a US envoy said, though the Russian leader said Washington must work with its European allies to understand if they want peace or war in Ukraine.

The move to give Europe a seat at the negotiating table at the next round of talks, which US envoy Steve Witkoff announced after the talks, could mark a breakthrough. But Putin’s comments underlined how difficult the negotiations could become, given sharp differences between Moscow and European capitals over the way the war should end.

“The Europeans will join at the next meeting, which we consider to be a very important moment because they are our partners and it’s important to us that they take part,” Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin in the Kremlin.

Show Full Article

Witkoff and fellow US presidential envoy Jared Kushner later flew to Ireland and met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who said he was pleased at the prospect of further sets of talks and European participation in them.

There were, however, signs of renewed tensions, with Zelenskiy saying new restrictions were affecting the US-made satellite communications Kyiv uses on the battlefield, and that he found the US approach of discussing a new European security order with Russia “a bit strange”.

EU ROLE IN TALKS?

During the Kremlin talks, Kushner told Putin that Washington had detected what he called “a big change” on the European side and was confident that expanding peace talks to include the Europeans would not hinder progress.

Putin said Moscow had always been open to talking to the EU about Ukraine, but signalled serious outstanding differences.

“As far as the Europeans are concerned, we have never been opposed to engaging in dialogue with Europe, and we have never broken off that dialogue. It was they who broke off the dialogue with the Russian Federation,” he said.

He then warned that the European idea of sending Western troops into Ukraine once a peace deal was concluded would trigger a resumption of the war because Russia would see that as a threat to its own security.

“We would very much like you, gentlemen, and the US administration as a whole, to work with your European allies so that they can finally make up their minds as to what they want: peace or war in Ukraine,” said Putin.

In a briefing after the talks, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov did not confirm that the Europeans would join the next round of peace talks and said their current stance on Ukraine amounted to “a recipe for endless war.”

After Zelenskiy’s brief discussions with the two US envoys in Ireland, the Ukrainian president welcomed news that Europeans would be present at the next round of peace talks and expressed hope that the agenda would include steps towards a ceasefire and de-escalating the conflict.

“It’s important that everything is unblocked,” Zelenskiy said, after meeting the envoys whilst in Dublin to attend a European summit.

“We decided that we will work on an agenda about any kind of de-escalation, some kind of ceasefires… I hope that we will have such agenda. Yes, this is important.”

The two days of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi this week were the first direct US-mediated negotiations between Russia and Ukraine in nine months.

Kyiv and Moscow said there had been some progress but that major differences remained, including on territorial issues. Russia holds about one-fifth of Ukraine and Kyiv refuses to give up the rest of the Donbas region in its east.

Earlier on Thursday, Zelenskiy said disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications service were significant, affecting the entire front line and Russian-controlled parts of Ukraine. Starshield is the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite communications service, and Ukraine suffered similar disruptions last month.

“So far we know very little (on the Starshield restrictions). But some things are already clear: if someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then it tells us where things are going,” he said.

In a post on Telegram, he said that systemic restrictions were limiting the speed at which Starshield could be used. SpaceX declined to comment.

PROPOSED AID MISSION

In Moscow, Putin told the US envoys that Russia was proposing a joint Russian-Ukrainian humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka in eastern Ukraine, which he said Moscow controlled, an assertion Ukraine has taken issue with in the past, saying it retains a presence there.

Putin said the mission could be modeled on an initiative that allowed residents to leave the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine at the end of last month and for aid to be brought in for those who chose to remain.

Russia needed five days to clear the area near Kostiantynivka of mines, Putin said, saying there were 400 to 500 city residents who were still there. The mission would allow the world to understand who controlled the city, he added.

Ushakov, the Kremlin aide, said the US envoys had welcomed Putin’s idea and would be in touch with Russia about it.

Kyiv has expressed concerns that Moscow might wish to use ceasefires for such missions to enable its military to regroup.

Moscow has not made major territorial gains this year, but has heavily attacked Ukrainian infrastructure and Kyiv has frequently struck Russian oil refineries with drones, causing fuel shortages over the summer, a problem which has resurfaced in some regions this week, according to local officials.

Putin has shown no signs of being ready to moderate his territorial demands, which include a buffer zone in parts of Ukraine which Russia has not formally claimed as its own. He said on Thursday that what Russia considers its state border should be the only meaningful demarcation point with Ukraine, in comments which appeared to signal his determination to pursue his aim of taking full control of all four Ukrainian regions that Moscow says it annexed in 2022.

(Reporting by Reuters; Additional reporting by Dmitry Antonov in Moscow, Maxim Rodionov in London, Daniel Flynn in Kyiv, Padraic Halpin in Dublin; Writing by Andrew Osborn; Editing by Timothy Heritage, Ron Popeski and Lincoln Feast.)

items.summary: US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Huang ...
items.body:
Home / World News / US lawmakers push for tougher curbs on advanced AI chip exports to China

US lawmakers push for tougher curbs on advanced AI chip exports to China US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Huang

The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 1:30 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Chinese AI shares tumbled on Friday, as investors worried that Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO could further restrict Chinese access to advanced US chips, deepening the technology divide between the world's two biggest economies.
  US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Huang, who has pushed to preserve access to the Chinese market and has close ties with US President Donald Trump.
  Huang stepped down after news reports of a romantic relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
 

  Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development.
  Senior White House officials were also discussing whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation said, as the desire to take action rose across Washington.
Also Read

Alice Huang had stake in China data centre serving Huawei, says report

  A growing number of lawmakers have criticized Lutnick for the administration's refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a US trade blacklist, and questioned whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia's exports to China.
  Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China's access to Nvidia's chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

  "The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here," Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favored limiting China's access to the advanced technology. "I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take."
  Investors dumped shares in Chinese AI models and hardware suppliers to the US on Friday, with AI model stocks Z.AI and MiniMax Group tumbling 12% and 8.4% respectively.
  Data center suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink Technology, whose businesses are heavily reliant on US markets, also slumped more than 8%.
  The Chinese businesswoman at the center of the scandal, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. 

REPUBLICANS EYE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS   The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions.
  Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company's chips remotely.
  Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defense 
authorization bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

  Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday. The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling.
  The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centers to access Nvidia chips. 
SCRUTINY OF HUANG LIKELY TO CONTINUE   Huang's resignation is unlikely to end congressional scrutiny of Nvidia and could leave the former chief executive more exposed to investigation, said Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation.

  "Congress can still subpoena him and Nvidia should conduct an independent investigation to determine whether the problems extend beyond Huang," Cheung said.
  Cheung said Huang's departure could weaken Nvidia's influence in Washington and create additional momentum for legislation that tightens restrictions on advanced chip exports. He said Nvidia's new leadership could also reconsider the company's China strategy as it seeks to rebuild trust with US policymakers.
  Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.

  Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with Alice Huang.

items.title: Allen Says US Needs Stronger Export-Control Enforcement
items.summary: Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, thinks Congress needs to direct its questions to the Commerce Department and, by extension, the National Security Council process staff about what happened with export-control regulations and what may have held them up. Allen says stronger export controls and beefing up the Department of Commerce are important, including greater enforcement, oversight and investigations. Allen says Trump should make clear to President Xi Jinping that China’s activity involving smuggling and restricted technology could lead Congress to take further action. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

Nov 12 : Nscale, a British cloud provider backed by chip giant Nvidia, amended its initial public offering filing on Thursday and said it expects revenue to jump 1,344 per cent in the first nine months of the year.
Here are more details:
• The London-based company reported preliminary revenue of $307.5 million in the nine months ended September 30, compared with revenue of $21.3 million in the year-ago period
• But it expects net loss of $1.7 billion in the reported period, wider than the $433.3 million net loss a year ago

• Thursday's amendment to the filing revealed the preliminary numbers after adding up the July-September quarter
• The company had revealed financials for the first six months of the year when it initially filed for the IPO in September
• The company was considering delaying the listing until next year, the Telegraph reported on Tuesday
• Nscale did not reveal the terms of the offering on Thursday
• The company provides infrastructure, including compute, power and data centers, as well as software for training and running AI models
• Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters for the offering. Nscale plans to list on the NYSE under the symbol "NSCL"

items.title: Perú eleva su tasa de interés al 4,50% por primera vez en casi cuatro años
items.author: Carla Samon Ros
items.summary: La inflación ha superado durante ocho meses consecutivos el límite superior del rango meta del banco central, del 3%, y se aceleró hasta el 5,25% en octubre, su mayor nivel desde 2023.
items.body: Bloomberg — Perú subió las tasas de interés por primera vez en casi cuatro años para contener un repunte de la inflación impulsado por el aumento de los precios de los alimentos y la energía. El jueves, el banco central elevó su tasa de referencia en 25 puntos básicos, hasta el 4,50%, en línea con las previsiones de la mayoría de los analistas consultados por Bloomberg . Solo dos de los 13 encuestados habían anticipado que no habría cambios. Ver más: Perú concreta la mayor emisión de bonos en dólares de su historia por US$4.500 millones La inflación ha superado durante ocho meses consecutivos el límite superior del rango meta del banco central, del 3%, y se aceleró hasta el 5,25% en octubre, su mayor nivel desde 2023. Aun así, Perú mantiene algunos de los niveles de inflación y costos de endeudamiento más bajos entre las principales economías de América Latina. El aumento de los precios internacionales de los combustibles y las alteraciones climáticas vinculadas al fenómeno de El Niño han encarecido el transporte y los alimentos. Se prevé que las presiones aumenten debido a las fuertes lluvias que amenazan la costa norte y la sequía que afecta al sur del país. El banco central tiene una meta de inflación de entre el 1% y el 3%, con un punto medio del 2%. El presidente de la entidad, Julio Velarde, elevó su previsión de inflación para 2026 al 4,2%, frente al 3,8% proyectado en septiembre, aunque prevé que el indicador regrese al rango meta en 2027, a medida que se disipen las presiones temporales. Ver más: ¿Qué esperar del precio del dólar en Perú en noviembre?: los dos escenarios que se proyectan para el sol Lea más en Bloomberg.com

FAST

WASHINGTON: United States House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday (Nov 12) there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang .
Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government. 
Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development.
Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

"The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here," Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China's access to the advanced technology. 
"I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take."
The Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed , an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Related:

Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?

Commentary: Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window

REPUBLICANS EYE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions.
Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company's chips remotely.  
Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defence authorisation Bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. 
Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four Bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday. 
The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling. 
The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centres to access Nvidia chips.
Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov 26. 
House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony. 
Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with the suspected Chinese spy.

items.title: Five things to know about APEC as Trump, Putin and Xi set to attend summit
items.summary: Founded as an informal 12-member dialogue effort in 1989 in the Australian capital Canberra, it has become the region's premier economic forum to foster ties on advancing growth, trade and investment ...
items.body:
Home / World News / Five things to know about APEC as Trump, Putin and Xi set to attend summit

Five things to know about APEC as Trump, Putin and Xi set to attend summit Founded as an informal 12-member dialogue effort in 1989 in the Australian capital Canberra, it has become the region's premier economic forum to foster ties on advancing growth, trade and investment

A worker pushes a row of trolleys past a promotion board for the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' meeting at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, in Shenzhen, China | Image: Reuters

Reuters HONG KONG 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 12:36 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Attention will focus next week on a summit of US, Chinese and Russian leaders set for the 21-member gathering of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China's southern technology hub of Shenzhen.
  WHAT IS APEC?  
      Founded as an informal 12-member dialogue effort in 1989 in the Australian capital of Canberra, it has become the region's premier economic forum to foster ties on advancing growth, trade and investment.
  Accounting for about 62% of global GDP and roughly half of global trade, the grouping of "member economies" rather than nations allows participation by Chinese-ruled Hong Kong and democratically governed Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its own territory.
 

  It does not include India, the world's most populous nation, however.
Also Read

Foreign businesses seized by Putin help fund Russia's war machine

Trump backed Huang despite spy allegations, urged him to fight for his job

Trump says ex Apple CEO Cook is 'a legend', should replace Huang at Nvidia

US returns over $12 bn in oil proceeds to Venezuela since Maduro's ouster

Trump says US doesn't need Iran deal, asks Vance to tackle corruption

  APEC operates on non-binding commitments reached strictly by consensus, with commitments undertaken on a voluntary basis.
  The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is set for November 18 and 19, preceded by an annual summit of CEOs on November 17-18.
  WHY SHENZHEN?  
  China is hosting the summit for the third time, after events in the commercial hub of Shanghai in 2001 and the capital, Beijing, in 2014.
  Both domestic and international reasons govern the choice of Shenzhen, adjacent to the financial centre of Hong Kong, said Chim Lee, senior analyst at the Economist Intelligence Unit.
  As part of China's Greater Bay Area home to Hong Kong and Macau, which Beijing seeks to establish as a global hub for technology and innovation, the city offers a platform to showcase China's vision for development and trade.

  It also highlights Shenzhen's resilience to geopolitical turbulence, Lee added.
  The city is the base of several leading Chinese auto and tech giants, such as BYD, Huawei and Tencent .
  WHO WILL BE THERE?  
  China has said President Xi Jinping will chair the leaders' meeting and deliver remarks. US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. are among those expected.
  The leaders of Canada, Australia, Mexico and Indonesia are also due to attend, along with those of Malaysia, South Korea and Vietnam among Asia-Pacific nations.
  Taiwan has designated Stan Shih, founder of Acer, as its envoy.
  Tokyo has not formally said whether Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will attend and New Zealand has not officially confirmed its delegation.

  WHAT TO WATCH AND KEY STICKING POINTS  
  West Asia Instability: The economic ripple effects of conflict, such as risks to energy security, trade flows, supply chains and inflation are major concerns expected to figure in talks.
  Tripartite Dynamics: All eyes are on the possible meeting of Chinese, Russian and US leaders. China is hesitant to engage in talks on nuclear disarmament, as it has fewer such weapons than the other two, analysts said.
  The US and Russia will also be keen to discuss the Ukraine war, but not necessarily China, they said.
  China-US Relations: A key focus to see if ties can stay stable. Both sides are falling short on commitments to an extended trade truce, analysts said. Rare earth supplies, artificial intelligence and tariffs are also likely to figure on the agenda, with US arms sales to Taiwan closely watched.

  China's ties with Japan and the Philippines: Strains in Japan and China ties have persisted since Prime Minister Takaichi angered Beijing in November 2025 by suggesting that Japan could deploy its military if a Chinese move against neighbouring Taiwan also threatened its territory.
  China-Philippines relations will likewise be closely watched amid continuing tension in the disputed waterway of the South China Sea.
  WHO ARE APEC'S MEMBERS?  
  These are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Peru, the Philippines, Russia, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, the United States and Vietnam.

items.title: SpiceJet to file overdue financial results after BSE warns of suspension
items.summary: SpiceJet's share of India's domestic aviation market, the world's third-largest, has plunged to just 0.6% from nearly 15% in 2019 ...
items.body:
Home / Companies / News / SpiceJet to file overdue financial results after BSE warns of suspension

SpiceJet to file overdue financial results after BSE warns of suspension SpiceJet's share of India's domestic aviation market, the world's third-largest, has plunged to just 0.6% from nearly 15% in 2019

The suspension will not take effect if SpiceJet complies with listing rules to the exchange's satisfaction by December 7, the notice said (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters NEW DELHI 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 12:35 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's SpiceJet said on Friday it will announce its overdue financial results by a December 7 deadline, days after one of the country's two main bourses warned it would suspend trading in shares of the cash-strapped airline if it failed to do so.
  SpiceJet's share of India's domestic aviation market, the world's third-largest, has plunged to just 0.6% from nearly 15% in 2019. The airline has slashed flights, grounded planes and delayed salary payments to many of its pilots amid a cash crunch that has forced it to seek government-backed financing.
  In a notice on Monday, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) in Mumbai said it would suspend trading in SpiceJet shares from December 10 because the airline had not filed its results for the March and June quarters.
 

  The suspension will not take effect if SpiceJet complies with listing rules to the exchange's satisfaction by December 7, the notice said.
  "The completion of audit has taken longer time and hence caused delay in filing of results," a SpiceJet spokesperson told Reuters, without explaining what delayed the audit.
Also Read

Recovery signals: Sensex valuation rebounds as November rally gathers pace premium

  The airline also said it had obtained an extension from the Registrar of Companies to hold its annual shareholder meeting for the financial year ended March 2026 by December 31. Under Indian law, companies must present their audited annual financial statements at such meetings.
  BSE said that during any suspension, the shares held by SpiceJet's controlling shareholders, along with other securities in their electronic securities accounts, would be frozen.

  SpiceJet's chairman and managing director, Ajay Singh, is among the airline's controlling shareholders. He did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
  Singh personally held a 12% stake as of March 31, while the wider group of controlling shareholders owned 24.2%, according to the company's latest available shareholding disclosure.
  SpiceJet competes with IndiGo and the Air India group, which together accounted for more than 90% of India's domestic passenger market in September. Its financial troubles have been worsened by the Middle East conflict, which has pushed up fuel prices and restricted airspace access.
  SpiceJet last reported financial results in February, posting a consolidated net loss of 2.62 billion rupees ($27.8 million) for the October-December 2025 quarter.

  Indian listing rules require companies to report quarterly results within 45 days of the end of each quarter, except the final quarter of the financial year, and audited annual results within 60 days of the financial year's end.
  Separately, SpiceJet said on Friday its board would meet on November 18 to consider raising fresh capital through the issuance of shares, debt securities or other financial instruments.

items.title: Ecopetrol disparó sus ganancias 85,6% en el tercer trimestre de 2026 y acumuló COP$13,7 billones a septiembre
items.author: Daniel Guerrero
items.summary: La petrolera registró mayores ingresos, EBITDA y utilidad neta frente al mismo periodo de 2025, favorecida por el incremento de los precios internacionales del petróleo y los márgenes de refinación.
items.body: Bogotá — Ecopetrol ( ECOPETL ) registró una utilidad neta de COP$4,76 billones durante el tercer trimestre de 2026, un crecimiento de 85,6% frente a los COP$2,56 billones reportados en el mismo periodo del año anterior. Con este resultado, la compañía acumuló ganancias por COP$13,71 billones en los primeros nueve meses del año, un incremento de 82,7% frente al mismo periodo de 2025. Ecopetrol. Símbolo: ECOPETL:CB. Clase de activo: equity. Los resultados estuvieron impulsados principalmente por un entorno internacional favorable para los precios del petróleo y los productos refinados, así como por mayores márgenes de comercialización. Estos factores compensaron parcialmente la menor producción, la reducción de los volúmenes vendidos y el efecto de una tasa de cambio promedio más baja. De acuerdo con el reporte financiero de la compañía, los ingresos por ventas alcanzaron COP$35,06 billones entre julio y septiembre, un aumento de 17,5% frente a los COP$29,84 billones del tercer trimestre de 2025. En el acumulado a septiembre, los ingresos llegaron a COP$103,89 billones, con un crecimiento de 14,3%. Por su parte, el resultado antes de intereses, impuestos, depreciaciones y amortizaciones (EBITDA) ascendió a COP$15,87 billones en el tercer trimestre, un incremento de 28,8% frente al mismo periodo del año anterior, cuando se ubicó en COP$12,33 billones. El margen EBITDA también mostró una mejora, al pasar de 41,3% a 45,3%. En los primeros nueve meses de 2026, este indicador alcanzó 45,2%, frente a 40,4% registrado en el mismo periodo de 2025. Uno de los principales factores detrás del desempeño financiero fue el comportamiento de los precios internacionales. El Brent promedió US$91,3 por barril durante el tercer trimestre de 2026, frente a US$68,2 del mismo periodo de 2025, lo que representó un incremento de 33,9%. La canasta combinada de venta de crudo y productos de Ecopetrol registró un precio promedio de US$110,3 por barril, un aumento de 49,9% frente al año anterior. En particular, la canasta de productos refinados alcanzó US$134,2 por barril, con un crecimiento de 64,3%, mientras que la de crudo se ubicó en US$82,2 por barril, un incremento de 27,8%. La compañía explicó que los mayores precios de referencia y los márgenes históricamente altos de los productos permitieron compensar el deterioro de los diferenciales comerciales de los crudos, la menor tasa de cambio promedio y la reducción de los volúmenes vendidos. En el caso de los productos refinados, el comportamiento estuvo relacionado con una menor oferta global, las disrupciones de suministro asociadas al conflicto en Oriente Medio, la reducción de inventarios y las paradas de refinerías en Rusia. Por segmentos, el negocio de refinación registró uno de los desempeños más destacados durante el tercer trimestre. Los ingresos por ventas de esta actividad llegaron a COP$21,97 billones, un crecimiento de 32,1% frente al mismo periodo de 2025. El EBITDA alcanzó COP$4,13 billones, frente a COP$783.000 millones del año anterior, mientras que la utilidad neta atribuible a los accionistas de Ecopetrol pasó de una pérdida de COP$178.000 millones a una ganancia de COP$2,25 billones. En los primeros nueve meses del año, el EBITDA de refinación alcanzó COP$9,12 billones, un aumento de 372,4%, mientras que la utilidad neta llegó a COP$4,23 billones. La compañía atribuyó estos resultados al entorno favorable de precios, los mayores rendimientos de productos de alto valor en las refinerías y la estrategia de maximización de cargas. Estos factores compensaron parcialmente los efectos de una menor tasa de cambio, el mayor costo de las materias primas y la parada integral programada de la Refinería de Barrancabermeja durante el tercer trimestre. El negocio de exploración, desarrollo y producción también presentó resultados positivos. Sus ingresos alcanzaron COP$18,34 billones en el tercer trimestre, un incremento de 5,5%, mientras que el EBITDA llegó a COP$7,40 billones, con un crecimiento de 18,6%. La utilidad neta atribuible a los accionistas de Ecopetrol en este segmento fue de COP$1,42 billones, un aumento de 2,2%. En contraste, el negocio de transmisión de energía y vías registró menores ingresos y EBITDA trimestrales. Sus ventas sumaron COP$3,82 billones, una reducción de 8,2%, y el EBITDA se ubicó en COP$1,99 billones, una caída de 20,3%. En el frente operativo, la producción consolidada del Grupo Ecopetrol alcanzó 747.300 barriles de petróleo equivalente por día durante el tercer trimestre, una disminución de 0,5% frente al mismo periodo de 2025. La cifra incluye la consolidación del 100% de la producción de Brava Energía, adquirida por Ecopetrol en agosto de 2026 . Sin esta incorporación, la producción neta atribuible al Grupo fue de 728.400 barriles diarios, una reducción de 3% frente al año anterior. La producción de gas natural y otros productos blancos cayó 8,6%, mientras que la de crudo aumentó 1,8% en términos consolidados. La compañía señaló que la menor producción internacional, especialmente en Permian, la declinación natural de campos del Piedemonte y La Guajira, y las restricciones operativas relacionadas con el manejo de agua en los Llanos explicaron parte del comportamiento. Por su parte, las ventas totales llegaron a 937.300 barriles equivalentes por día, una disminución de 1,9% frente al tercer trimestre de 2025. Otro de los aspectos relevantes del balance fue el crecimiento de la deuda del grupo, relacionado principalmente con la adquisición de Brava Energía y las nuevas obligaciones asumidas para financiar la operación. Al cierre de septiembre de 2026, la deuda total de Ecopetrol llegó a COP$119,5 billones, equivalentes a US$36.076 millones. Esto representó un incremento de COP$14,6 billones frente al cierre de junio. La compañía explicó que el aumento estuvo relacionado con la incorporación de COP$12,3 billones de deuda de Brava Energía, un crédito de la banca internacional por US$1.173 millones para financiar la adquisición y nuevas obligaciones en otras compañías del grupo, principalmente ISA. Pese al incremento, el indicador de deuda bruta sobre EBITDA se ubicó en 2,1 veces, por debajo del límite de 2,5 veces establecido para 2026. La relación entre deuda neta y EBITDA fue de 1,9 veces. En cuanto a la liquidez, Ecopetrol cerró el tercer trimestre con una caja consolidada de COP$16,3 billones, incluidos COP$3,1 billones aportados por Brava Energía. Durante los primeros nueve meses de 2026, el Grupo Ecopetrol realizó inversiones orgánicas por US$4.766 millones, equivalentes a COP$16,7 billones. El 65% de estos recursos se destinó a operaciones en Colombia y el 35% restante a actividades internacionales. El negocio de hidrocarburos concentró US$3.077 millones, equivalentes al 65% del total. De ese monto, US$2.495 millones se destinaron a exploración y producción. Por su parte, las inversiones en transmisión de energía y vías sumaron US$1.284 millones, mientras que las destinadas a energías para la transición alcanzaron US$405 millones. Adicionalmente, la compañía realizó inversiones inorgánicas por US$1.400 millones, principalmente por la adquisición de Brava Energía en Brasil, por US$1.200 millones, y la compra de participación en Madeira, en ISA Brasil, por US$200 millones

items.body:
IRGC says destruction of US radar in Bahrain was warning to Washington, threatens harsher response to further violations "The destruction of a US radar in Bahrain was a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. If the enemy repeats its violations and acts of aggression, the IRGC Aerospace Force is on full alert to respond without limits," the IRGC said, as reported by Fars News Agency.
ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 12:29 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 12:29 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has claimed that its Aerospace Force destroyed a US early warning radar installation in Bahrain, describing the strike as a serious warning to Washington and threatening a harsher response if the United States repeats what Tehran calls acts of aggression and violations. According to Fars News Agency, the IRGC said the radar was targeted and destroyed in retaliation for an alleged US aerial attack on a telecommunications tower in Iran's Sirik region. The force claimed that its personnel carried out the strike on the US military's early warning radar on Bahrain Island approximately an hour after the attack.
In a statement, the IRGC said the destruction of the radar was intended to warn the United States against continuing its aerial operations and what it described as oil smuggling in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. "The destruction of a US radar in Bahrain was a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. If the enemy repeats its violations and acts of aggression, the IRGC Aerospace Force is on full alert to respond without limits," the IRGC said, as reported by Fars News Agency.
The force further warned companies against falling for what it called the enemy's deception, saying those that did so would face harsher penalties. The latest warning comes amid escalating tensions between Iran, the United States and Israel, with the Strait of Hormuz emerging as a key flashpoint in the confrontation. The narrow waterway is a major route for global oil shipments, making security in the region a significant international concern.
Earlier, Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei warned countries against providing military or logistical assistance to Washington for its operations against Tehran, saying any direct or indirect involvement would be considered participation in aggression against Iran. In a post on X, Baqaei invoked the United Nations Charter and international law while cautioning governments against supporting US military operations.
“A sparrow that tries to fly after a stork will eventually break its legs (Korean proverb),” he said, warning countries against aligning themselves with Washington's military actions. Baqaei said, “Any direct or indirect involvement in acts of aggression or in inhumane economic terrorism against Iran - including the deployment of naval forces, military and logistical support equipment, and personnel - will be regarded as a hostile and unlawful act amounting to participation in the US aggression against Iran. Such actions not only violate Article 2 (4) of the Charter of the United Nations but also fall within the definition of an act of aggression set out in UN General Assembly Resolution 3314.”
Rejecting possible justifications for such assistance, he said, “Invoking seemingly legitimate pretexts such as ‘protecting freedom of navigation’ or ‘countering piracy’ does not alter the unlawful and hostile nature of such actions.” “Our message is unequivocal: No bilateral agreement or commitment with the United States can constitute legitimate grounds for violating a state's obligations under international law or for participating in the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran,” Baqaei added.
He further warned that any state participating in such actions would bear full responsibility for the consequences. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump, in an interview with Salem News Channel on Thursday (local time), issued a warning to Tehran over any potential threat to American officials.
“They will not exist any longer,” Trump said when asked about the possibility of Iran killing US officials, adding that he would have “no hesitation” in using military force. Trump also claimed that the United States had total control over the Strait of Hormuz and said that the Iranian regime was collapsing. (ANI)

items.title: Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval
items.summary: TL;DR: Russian exchanges may begin cryptocurrency trading from November 22 if their trading rules receive the Bank of Russia’s concurrence. The November 11 announcement sets operating requirements for ...
items.body:
News
/ NewsBTC
/ Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval

Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval 3 min read

BTCUSD ETHUSD USDTUSD
TL;DR: Russian exchanges may begin cryptocurrency trading from November 22 if their trading rules receive the Bank of Russia’s concurrence. The November 11 announcement sets operating requirements for venues. A separate asset-eligibility ordinance takes effect on November 17, so the two dates describe different regulatory steps.
Russia has added another piece to its regulated crypto market framework, with a new ordinance setting the conditions under which exchanges can start trading digital currencies and digital rights. The Bank of Russia’s November 11 notice identifies November 22 as the earliest start under those rules, subject to the regulator agreeing to a venue’s trading arrangements.
That condition matters. An effective date creates a legal opening; it does not show that every exchange is technically ready or that every prospective customer can place an order on the same morning.
The exchange rulebook comes into focus
Under the announcement, exchanges must register trading participants, maintain records of orders and transactions, and monitor trading. They also have to calculate specified prices and report trading information to the central bank using the procedures applied to other assets.
These requirements address the organisation of a market: who participates, how activity is recorded and what the supervisor can inspect. The notice says the Ministry of Justice has registered the ordinance. It does not name a completed launch at a particular exchange or provide a forecast for trading volumes.
Why November 17 is a different milestone
The central bank’s November 6 asset-eligibility announcement set a November 17 effective date for an ordinance covering Bitcoin, Ether and USDT. That notice deals with which assets non-qualified investors may access and the conditions attached to their purchases.
Non-qualified investors face an annual purchase ceiling of 300,000 rubles through a single intermediary. Qualified investors are not subject to that asset-list and purchase-limit restriction. The central bank says investors in both groups must pass the relevant test and familiarise themselves with crypto investment risks before transacting.
Reading the announcements together avoids a misleading single-date headline. One concerns the eligible assets and investor conditions; the other concerns organised trading requirements. Neither removes the need to check when a particular intermediary actually makes a service available.
Domestic permission and platform access differ
A national regulatory opening can exist alongside changes at individual international exchanges. NewsBTC previously reported KuCoin’s withdrawal from Russia and Belarus, where affected users’ account notices determine their closure deadlines.
Those developments should be assessed separately. A domestic venue’s permission does not change another company’s service terms, and an international exchange exit does not by itself tell us when a domestic alternative will be usable.
For a trader, the practical questions include the identity of the intermediary, the assets it supports, how a purchase is funded and where holdings are kept. For an exchange, reliable records and price calculations become part of delivering a functioning service rather than merely announcing one.
A new route does not measure new demand
The market impact depends on participation after services open. An expanded route into Bitcoin could bring additional buyers, but it could also shift activity from one channel to another. Permission alone cannot distinguish those outcomes or establish how much fresh capital will arrive.
There is a longer institutional backdrop. NewsBTC reported VTB’s conditional plans for direct crypto trading in December 2025. That historical proposal helps explain interest in domestic access, but it is not evidence that the bank has launched a service under the latest rules.
The next meaningful evidence from Russia will be venue-specific launch notices, completed onboarding and observable trading activity. Until those arrive, November 22 is best understood as a conditional regulatory starting point. It is a material step toward an organised market, with implementation still determining what customers can actually do.
written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

items.title: World shares are mixed as Nvidia's troubles weigh on AI stocks
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: World shares were mixed on Thursday as concerns over leadership at chipmaker Nvidia weighed on artificial intelligence-related stocks.
items.body: NEW YORK — The U.S. stock market shook Thursday, but it largely absorbed big swings for Nvidia and oil prices and finished with relatively modest losses. The moves suggested Wall Street sees limited fallout for the artificial intelligence industry, which carries immense influence on the market, despite the sudden fall of one of its biggest evangelists. After dropping nearly one per cent at the start of trading, the S&P 500 quickly erased all of the loss before finishing with a dip of 0.4 per cent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 189 points, or 0.4 per cent, while the Nasdaq composite sank 0.4 per cent after trimming an early drop of 1.6 per cent. Stocks broadly felt pressure from a rise in oil prices after U.S. President Donald Trump said he’s no longer interested in a deal with Iran to end their war. Instead of that, Trump said he asked his vice president to investigate U.S. cities and states run by Democrats. On a typical day, that could be the main driver of action on Wall Street. But little has been typical recently for the yo-yoing stock market. The focus instead was on Nvidia’s stock. It plunged 14 per cent at the start of trading following the resignation of Jensen Huang, its CEO, co-founder and face of the brand. The chip company’s stock has been sinking since its board announced an investigation into Huang for a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese government agent. It’s a stunning fall for Huang and for Nvidia, which had become Wall Street’s most valuable and influential stock because of its central role in the AI boom. Its stock price set a record last month after soaring an astounding 1,722 per cent in four years. That compares with the already healthy gain of nearly 109 per cent for the overall S&P 500 over the same time. But Nvidia’s price dropped 27 per cent from then through Wednesday. At first, the drop was because of worries about too-high prices for stocks across the AI industry. More recently, it’s been due to worries about whether Huang would remain as CEO and how Nvidia would navigate a future without him. Nvidia’s board answered the first question Thursday morning, when it said Huang resigned, and it named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as its interim CEO. The second question remains unanswered. And it looms over the entire market because Nvidia and the broader AI industry have been the main reasons the U.S. stock market has set so many records in recent years. Nvidia, to be sure, is still selling AI chips at a quick rate regardless of who stands on a stage and talks them up, and analysts said it remains the industry’s leader. That helped Nvidia quickly halve its early loss Thursday, and its stock finished with a fall of 4.3 per cent. That paring helped the broader market to recover. Outside of Nvidia, stocks across the AI industry swung in the uncertainty. CoreWeave, which buys Nvidia chips and then rents out access to them to customers over the cloud, fell 6.9 per cent. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers that’s been getting gobbled up in the AI frenzy, sank 1.6 per cent. But Broadcom rose 5.5 per cent, and Advanced Micro Devices added 5.9 per cent on hopes the rival chip companies will gain a competitive advantage. Those two gains came close to offsetting the drop for Nvidia, which was the single heaviest weight on the S&P 500. That suggests investors see the AI business expanding to other players rather than depending solely on Nvidia. Also helping to limit the U.S. market’s losses were gains for stocks in the oil and gas industry. Marathon Petroleum climbed 2.5 per cent, and ExxonMobil added 1.8 per cent. They benefited from a rise in oil prices after Trump said on his social media platform, “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” The price for a barrel of Brent crude climbed 3.3 per cent to US$95.82. The price for the most actively traded contract in the Brent market has been veering sharply since the United States and Israel began the war with Iran in late February, bouncing between roughly US$70 and US$120. Higher oil prices push up worries about inflation, and the yield on the 10-year Treasury jumped to 5.12 per cent from 4.98 per cent late Tuesday. Trading in the bond market had been closed Wednesday for Veterans Day. Higher yields make borrowing money more expensive for everyone, from the U.S. government to companies building AI data centres to regular people buying houses. High mortgage rates helped send sales of previously occupied U.S. homes in October to their slowest pace in more than 16 years. The housing industry has been slowing the U.S. economy but not upending it. A separate report on Thursday said that slightly more U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week, but the number remains relatively low compared with history. All told, the S&P 500 fell 26.98 points to 7,592.40. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 189.40 to 52,297.09, and the Nasdaq composite sank 100.10 to 25,366.09. In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed in Europe following a weaker finish in Asia. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.3 per cent for one of the world’s biggest moves. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Business Writer Yuri Kageyama contributed to this report.

By Maria Tsvetkova
NEW YORK, Nov 12 (Reuters) – Rescue teams worked through torrential rain on Thursday in search of victims still buried in the rubble of a New York City apartment building collapse that killed at least eight people and prompted Mayor Zohran Mamdani to order an investigation into dozens of linked construction sites.

A day after Wednesday’s late-afternoon collapse in the city’s Brooklyn borough, Mamdani said the city would examine five companies associated with a construction site adjacent to the collapse and 100 more sites connected with those entities.

The construction site was undergoing excavation work that started earlier this year, historical satellite imagery showed. An official notice filed by a construction company in September informed authorities that the earthwork included “rock blasting,” official records showed.

Show Full Article

Six people were found dead in the wreckage and two others died later from their injuries, city officials told reporters at the scene of the collapse. Two of those killed were children. The six adults killed included two construction workers.

Those injured in the collapse and its aftermath stood at 18, including four of the firefighters who led the rescue effort, officials said.

Municipal building inspectors fanned out across the city to conduct inspections of the other sites “to ensure that if there is anything for New Yorkers to be worried about that we are on the scene and we are doing something about it,” the mayor said at a press conference.

“If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them fully accountable,” Mamdani said.

The apartment building, which Mamdani said was home to several immigrant families, was built in 1930 and consisted of four residential units, according to official records. Two Ecuadoreans were among the dead.

The building collapsed around 4 p.m. (2100 GMT) on Wednesday and destroyed a wall of an adjacent residential block, exposing a staircase, closets and a bedroom.

Three other addresses were ordered vacated on the same side of the street as a precaution until safety inspections could be conducted, officials said.

On Thursday, two excavators were seen at the construction site clearing the debris under pouring rain. Mamdani said rescue work by some 250 personnel was continuing around the clock.”We will be here until we are 100% sure there are no more people trapped,” Fire Department Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore told reporters. “We always assume that there are more people there until we can access the ground. So until we remove some of the bigger debris and are able to search beneath them, this will remain a rescue operation.”

(Reporting by Maria Tsvetkova in New York; Additional reporting by Steve Gorman in Los Angeles and Jonathan Allen in New York; Editing by Howard Goller)
