items.title: Would a Tesla–SpaceX Merger Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Careful What You Wish For
items.summary: As speculation about a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger continues to bubble, cryptocurrency market observers are asking a crucial question: could it drain liquidity from Bitcoin CRYPTO:BTCUSD the way ...
items.body:
News
/ Benzinga
/ Would a Tesla–SpaceX Merger Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Careful What You Wish For

Would a Tesla–SpaceX Merger Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Careful What You Wish For 2 min read

BTCUSD SPCX TSLA BTCUSD
As speculation about a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger continues to bubble, cryptocurrency market observers are asking a crucial question: could it drain liquidity from Bitcoin BTCUSD the way SpaceX’s SPCX IPO once did?
A Merger Wouldn’t Trigger the Same Bitcoin Selling an IPO Did
Benzinga reported in October how analyst Benjamin Cowen previously linked Bitcoin’s weakness ahead of SpaceX’s IPO to softness before Anthropic’s expected listing. His theory: investors were holding back capital for the next big offering.
GSR’s Spencer Hallarn made a similar point to Reuters in June, saying "crypto is a funding currency for a lot of this" as investors weighed SpaceX’s planned $75 billion raise.
A merger would work differently from an IPO, since RBC’s hypothetical all-stock model has Tesla TSLA shareholders simply swapping their shares for SpaceX shares and no cash required.
With nothing to buy, there’s no reason for investors to sell Bitcoin to fund it.
SpaceX and Tesla’s Combined Bitcoin Stash Isn’t the Risk It Looks Like
Tesla’s latest quarterly filing confirms an independent committee is exploring a closer relationship with SpaceX, including a possible business combination, though the company cautions no deal is assured.
Here’s what the two companies actually hold in Bitcoin:
SpaceX: 18,712 BTC, unchanged since December 2025
Tesla: 11,509 BTC, also unchanged
Combined: 30,221 BTC, worth $2.53 billion at Bitcoin’s September 30 close of $83,553.85, now worth roughly $2.16 billion, a $370 million decline
That drop has nothing to do with a merger. It’s just Bitcoin’s price falling since the quarter closed.
SpaceX spent $48.07 billion on property and equipment over the first nine months against $13.10 billion in operating cash flow, a gap that might suggest pressure to raise cash.
But the company still held $89.86 billion in cash and securities at quarter-end, which undercuts any theory that capex spending alone would force SpaceX to sell its Bitcoin.
Meanwhile, Polymarket currently prices a formal merger announcement at 54% by June 30, 2027, and 68% by year-end 2027.
Could Huang Joining SpaceX Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Not Yet
Elon Musk replied it “would be an honor" to a ZeroHedge post urging him to hire Jensen Huang , with Polymarket traders now pricing roughly 8% to 10% odds Huang joins SpaceX by year-end.
If that hire happened, it could arguably be a modest bullish signal for Bitcoin specifically, since SpaceX already holds 18,712 BTC on its balance sheet and adding a high-profile AI leader could reinforce investor confidence in the company managing that treasury alongside its broader business.
That theory didn’t play out Thursday, though as SpaceX shares rose about 2%, while Bitcoin fell roughly 3% alongside the broader AI and chip stock selloff.
The split shows Bitcoin and SpaceX stock barely move each other right now, since the $2.2 billion crypto holding is a rounding error against a company worth well over $1.5 trillion. Disclaimer Preview Image: Shutterstock

By David Brunnstrom

WASHINGTON, Nov 12 (Reuters) – The leader of Tibet’s government-in-exile expressed disappointment that human rights appeared absent from US President Donald Trump’s dealings with China, telling Reuters that a focus solely on trade and business risked emboldening Beijing.

Penpa Tsering said in an interview on Wednesday night that US support for Tibet remained broadly stable under the Trump administration, but Tibet was not on the agenda at the presidential level as Washington focuses on trade, security and other priorities with China.

Show Full Article

“(Trump) has never mentioned Tibet, he has never mentioned human rights,” he said during a visit to Washington.

China seized control of Tibet in 1950 in what it describes as a “peaceful liberation” from feudalistic serfdom.

International human rights groups and exiles have routinely condemned what they call China’s oppressive rule in Tibetan areas, assessments Beijing rejects.

Tsering said the US remained the Tibetan exile movement’s most important international partner and Tibet enjoyed strong bipartisan backing in Congress.

He said his Central Tibetan Administration continued to engage with the State Department, and noted that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was a longtime champion of Tibet-related legislation when he was a senator.

While State Department foreign assistance cuts halved money for Tibet last year, Tsering expressed optimism that full funding would be restored later this year and noted that the current Trump administration appointed a special coordinator for Tibetan issues in its second year, compared with the fourth year of Trump’s first term.

TIBET UNLIKELY TO FEATURE IN TRUMP-XI TALKS

Tsering said he did not expect Tibet to feature in Trump’s planned meetings with Chinese leader Xi Jinping at next week’s APEC summit or at the G20 summit in Florida next month and suggested this may be preferable to becoming a bargaining chip in broader US-China negotiations.

“Maybe sometimes it’s better that way,” he said. “Instead of becoming a bargaining chip. And China is very good in creating leverages.” 

However, he said Western governments had become overly focused on trade and economic ties with China while neglecting rights concerns, strengthening China’s power in the process.

“Knowing that the dragon is biting at you, if you still keep feeding them, then whose fault is it?” he said. 

“We should be talking more on balancing trade … with human rights and other things, which is not happening so much these days, unfortunately, even people who accuse America of backsliding on democracy still suck up to China.”

He highlighted China’s “ethnic unity and progress” policies, saying they were aimed at weakening Tibetan identity, language, religion and culture. He said Chinese authorities were becoming more open about assimilation policies and faced little international pushback.

China does not recognize the exiled government and has defended its rule in Tibet as bringing much-needed development to what was a backward and feudal society.

(Reporting by David Brunnstrom; Editing by Don Durfee and Sanjeev Miglani)

items.title: Canada-U.S. travel turnoff reversing after U.S. midterm elections
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Travel experts say the Democrats’ sweeping midterm victory is poised to fan a trend of rising Canadian visitor volumes to the United States.
items.body: MONTREAL — The Democrats’ sweeping midterm victory is poised to fan a trend of rising Canadian visitor volumes to the United States, counteracting the effect of the recent trade war flare-up, travel experts say. Canadian return trips from America rose three per cent in October compared with the same period last year, the seventh-straight month of growth, according to preliminary figures from Statistics Canada. However, the increase marked a smaller uptick than the levels seen through much of the summer and into September. At Flight Centre Travel Group Canada, new leisure bookings — distinct from trips taken — fell 26 per cent year-over-year last month in response to a fresh round of tariffs and taunts by U.S. President Donald Trump weeks earlier. “It really just shows you how fragile cross-border travel is, specifically from the leisure market,” said Amra Durakovic, a spokesperson for the travel agency. Over the past week though, Flight Centre has seen signs of a return to the Canada-U.S. tourism rebound in the wake of the Democrats’ electoral success on Nov. 3, widely viewed as a rebuke to White House policies. “We are hearing a degree of cautious optimism from some travellers who were reluctant to return,” Durakovic said. “One customer, he booked a Mississippi River cruise, and they did that instead of exploring another European holiday,” she said. “Tuesday’s election, that influenced their decision. They said that they definitely feel a lot more comfortable travelling to the U.S. now.” For now, Canadian visitor volumes remain far below levels from 2024 — 27 per cent below in October — as the trade war drags on and Canadians opt for other destinations. Nonetheless, the torrent of votes for Democratic candidates from Kansas to the Carolinas set off flickers of a possible revival in stateside travel, or perhaps signs of what a Democratic triumph in 2028 could herald for tourism. “Pickup to the U.S. has happened in the last week — people that weren’t going to go,” said Marty Firestone, noting an abrupt rise in business at the insurance firm he heads, Travel Secure Inc. “There was a real bad feeling last year: ‘I’m not going there. That man doesn’t want us. He calls us the 51st state,’” Firestone said, describing the attitude of many Canadians. “With the Democratic blue tsunami, as they call it, I think that Canadians are somewhat feeling a little more relieved about going back to the U.S.” Others say it’s too early to gauge whether the midterms revamped interest in cross-border trips. “We need at least a month,” said Richard Vanderlubbe, who heads Hamilton-based travel agency Tripcentral.ca. Even if an upward shift is underway, he suspects it’s a minor one, with Trump set to remain in the Oval Office for two more years. “I don’t feel like there’s a sea change. It’s not like the phones lit up on Wednesday morning with emails flying and, ‘Hey, OK, it’s good to go to the States now.’” The ill feeling is strong enough that some travel agencies avoid promoting American packages altogether. “We just don’t know which of our customers is going to be wildly offended by any kind of marketing in the United States … so we just don’t do it,” Vanderlubbe said. “To market the U.S. is like dynamite.” Flight volumes from Canada to Florida, Arizona, Nevada and California are down 17 per cent in total this quarter versus the final three months of 2024, according to aviation data firm Cirium. Overall Canada-U.S. flight volumes decreased only 10 per cent, revealing the bigger drop in demand for sun-splashed leisure hot spots. Corporate travel continues to hum along, Durakovic said, with virtually no drop in Flight Centre bookings over the past couple of years. “It’s still business as usual. You can’t exactly stop travelling to the U.S. because of politics,” she said. The broader Canadian aversion to travelling south of the border combined with the shutdown of Cuban resorts amid a fuel shortage caused by an American oil blockade has pushed sun seekers farther afield. Mexico, the Dominican Republic and Jamaica have surged in popularity, travel agents said. Portugal and Spain have also enjoyed a recent boost in Canadian visitors. “Air Transat flights to Malaga are full,” said Sal Lato, who owns the Voyages Marlin travel agency franchise. Meanwhile, the leisure airline has cut the 36 flights a week it operated between Canada and Florida in late 2024 down to zero. Not all winter escapees can simply point their finger at a fresh spot on the map and jet off for a getaway, extended or otherwise. “There are still deep ties to many U.S. snowbird destinations,” said Stephen Fine, founder of Snowbird Advisor Insurance. “They have friends who’ve been going there for years and they want to be able to spend their winters with that community,” he said of many Canadians. “A lot of them own properties there. People want to drive down to their destination or have their vehicles with them for the winter,” he noted. For them, America may be the only option. --- Christopher Reynolds, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 12, 2026.

items.title: Investor Outlook: Nvidia’s AI demand offers cushion after Huang’s exit
items.author: BNN Bloomberg
items.summary: Nvidia faces a leadership transition as Kim Forrest discusses the chipmaker’s next chapter and the implications for AI stocks.
items.body: Jensen Huang’s departure puts Nvidia’s next chapter in focus, raising questions about how the AI chipmaker will evolve under new leadership. BNN Bloomberg spoke with Kim Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners, about the transition and what it could mean for the semiconductor sector. Key Takeaways Read the full transcript below: ROGER: Nvidia shares are under pressure with the news that CEO Jensen Huang is resigning amid allegations surrounding a second extramarital affair. Investors are now grappling with what leadership uncertainty could mean for one of the world’s most valuable companies, possibly one of the most powerful companies, a leader in the AI race. Joining us now is Kim Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners. Kim, thanks very much for joining us today. KIM: It’s a pleasure. ROGER: OK, we’re seeing the reaction, but the — it seems to be tempered a little bit, a little more now. I mean, earlier today, when the news first broke on the — on the premarket, it was down about 10 per cent. Now we’re off about 4.8, 4.9. How are people approaching this? How are you approaching it? KIM: Well, I think you really have to look at how big of a company we’re talking about here. It’s not a one-person company. That is the good news. The other thing is, is this is one of the companies that’s supplying AI. It is a huge driver, of course, of everything AI. But again, the companies who are buying their products are the ones that are sort of driving where the product goes, not the company driving where the models go. So if you look at it that way, and you realize that their production is sold out a year ahead of time, you have relatively low risk here for the company not meeting its financial objectives. It also looks like there is a bench of people that can take over, at least in the interim. And I think it’ll be interesting who the board picks as the next CEO. Nvidia has always been a very narrow company. First, for most of its life, it did video, you know, chips, and now it has branched out into other areas that use that technology in different ways. So what could Nvidia become? Only the next CEO knows. ROGER: There is — there is a lot ahead. Now you mentioned that it’s more than just Huang’s Nvidia, but he was perceived as a rock star and kind of — and he’s the face of it. And he had that unique arrangement. I mean, 60 people reported directly to him. Is that — are those things easy to overcome? KIM: Well, we’re going to find out. But look at his schedule. I think that gives you a peek into what the company was really doing. He has been doing a lot of press, a lot of conferences, flying around the world. That’s some of the issues that probably got him into the trouble that he’s in. That he wasn’t back at the company, you know, minding the store. So I’m thinking that the company probably is well positioned internally to do what it does, which is make the chip that every AI frontier lab wants to have. And I think that is important for investors to remember whenever they see the stock price falling. ROGER: OK, now for a replacement, we’ve got Colette Kress, temporary. The CFO is now in as CEO. Is she a possibility, or will they look outside, do you think? KIM: Well, the company itself has said internal and external candidates are being looked at, and I believe she has a pretty good shot at retaining that. Now we will certainly see, and I think the board, because it doesn’t look great for them that these issues have come up, and it doesn’t sound like they were really on top of, you know, being a board of directors, knowing what the management is doing, so I think they’re going to be very careful about who they choose as CEO. Although they have to really start getting down to the work here shortly. ROGER: And I want to ask: They also appointed Harvey Jones as the chair, and they’ve never had a chair before. What does that — does that mean anything to you, or is it — can we read into it? KIM: Well, absolutely. I mean, you know, Jensen Huang was the company. He was the chairman of the board. He was the CEO, and, you know, in a lot of governance circles, that is a warning sign that there’s too much power in one person. So I think it’s good that they did not, you know, keep that arrangement. But I don’t think it’s practical either. So I think having a separated CEO and board chair is probably what a lot of companies should think about doing, and just spread the risk around and make people more accountable. ROGER: All right, just doing some quick math. Down about 17 per cent. Is Nvidia a buying opportunity, or is it AMD or something like that? KIM: Well, I think a lot of companies are. I’m a bull on the longer-term aspects of AI. I am somebody who doesn’t believe that the leading frontier labs are going to be game over, the winners in the long run. So I think there is a lot of opportunity out there, and we like to spread the risk around and not just have one holding being the AI chip. So we like AMD, we like Micron and we like Nvidia. ROGER: Any concerns about the chips from a government perspective, that they may put in restriction or further restrictions on what — who can buy the chips, what, when and where? KIM: Well, I think everybody’s going to take a good, hard look at that. So yes, I would think that there are some — we’ll just say clarifications coming to the export laws, especially in these — in AI chips. ROGER: All right, and you mentioned the numbers are pretty solid. What are you going to be looking for next week with that — that earnings report? What will be a key number for you? KIM: Well, it’s really what the bookings are going to be, you know, beyond a year ahead. What do the bookings look like? You know, we’ve been using this as a measure of: Is AI healthy? Looking at the semiconductors, things are turning. I think Anthropic, with it being public, is going to be the new face of AI health. Are people buying their product, which is a service to do, you know, whatever they do with it, write code, you know, create agents, whatever? So I think the importance of Nvidia being the indicator of health in AI spending is going to change, and I think that’s probably a good thing. ROGER: OK, we have to wrap it up there, Kim. But always appreciate talking to you. Thanks very much for joining us. KIM: Thank you. ROGER: Kim Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners. --- This BNN Bloomberg summary and transcript of the Nov. 12, 2026 interview with Kim Forrest are published with the assistance of AI. Original research, interview questions and added context was created by BNN Bloomberg journalists. An editor also reviewed this material before it was published to ensure its accuracy and adherence with BNN Bloomberg editorial policies and standards.

items.title: De Lisa Su a un ejecutivo de Apple: los posibles candidatos para reemplazar a Jensen Huang en Nvidia
items.author: Brody Ford, Ian King, Nina Trentmann
items.summary: La compañía contrató a una firma externa para identificar posibles sucesores. Entre los perfiles que podrían entrar en la búsqueda figuran ejecutivos de AMD, Arm, Apple, Amazon y Google.
items.body: Bloomberg — Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) busca un sustituto permanente para su carismático exCEO, Jensen Huang, un reto formidable en el fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo. La compañía contrató a una empresa externa para identificar posibles candidatos tras las revelaciones de relaciones extramatrimoniales por parte de Huang. Sin embargo, encontrar un reemplazo no será fácil: durante más de tres décadas, ha combinado una profunda experiencia técnica con habilidades operativas en un rol inusualmente activo en la configuración de la estrategia de Nvidia. Además de desarrollar los aceleradores de IA que ahora dominan el panorama de la inteligencia artificial, Huang ha convertido a la empresa en un actor clave en la industria, que supervisa una extensa red de clientes, proveedores, socios e inversiones. Ver más: Jensen Huang renuncia como CEO de Nvidia tras escándalo por infidelidades Por ahora, la veterana directora financiera Colette Kress ejerce como CEO interina. Asumió el cargo el jueves tras la renuncia de Huang. Aquí un resumen de los ejecutivos que probablemente acaben en el punto de mira de un cazatalentos: Kress es la ejecutiva más conocida de Nvidia, además de Huang, al menos entre los inversores. Los consejos de administración suelen recurrir a los directores financieros para lograr una estabilización a corto plazo, aunque generalmente se les considera una solución provisional más que una opción a largo plazo, especialmente en las empresas tecnológicas. El vicepresidente Ian Buck dirige los productos de Nvidia para centros de datos, como sus chips de IA. Es una figura conocida para los clientes de Nvidia y, además, es el inventor de CUDA, el marco de software que permite que sus chips sean útiles para la IA. Sin embargo, carece de la experiencia operativa que los inversores suelen buscar en la dirección de una gran empresa que cotiza en bolsa. El CEO de Arm Holdings Plc ( ARM ), René Haas, supervisa una empresa líder en diseño de chips con una estrecha colaboración con Nvidia. Exejecutivo de Nvidia, Haas ahora gestiona un complejo ecosistema de clientes y socios, con un conocimiento profundo del fabricante de chips de IA y del panorama tecnológico en general. En 2020, Nvidia incluso intentó adquirir Arm —una empresa de SoftBank Group Corp.— en una operación que fracasó tras un análisis antimonopolio. Lisa Su, CEO de Advanced Micro Devices Inc. ( AMD ), lidera al competidor más cercano de Nvidia en cuanto a la tecnología que ofrece y la cartera de clientes a la que atiende. Bajo su dirección, AMD superó a Intel Corp. ( INTC ), pionera en la fabricación de chips, en liderazgo tecnológico, y sus acciones se han multiplicado casi por 170. Sin embargo, AMD es mucho más pequeña que Nvidia y sus chips de IA aún tienen un largo camino por recorrer antes de alcanzar la adopción de Nvidia. Johny Srouji, director de hardware de Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), ha liderado uno de los programas de desarrollo de chips internos más exitosos de la industria, supervisando los chips personalizados que impulsan el iPhone, el Mac y otros dispositivos de Apple. Su trayectoria le otorga una gran credibilidad en el diseño de chips, la integración de productos y las hojas de ruta tecnológicas a largo plazo. Sin embargo, gran parte de su experiencia se ha forjado dentro del ecosistema estrictamente controlado de Apple, y no ha sido puesto a prueba en el tipo de ventas de alto perfil por las que Huang es famoso. Ver más: Trump propone a Tim Cook para reemplazar a Jensen Huang en Nvidia: “Una leyenda reemplaza a otra leyenda” El presidente Donald Trump también barajó la idea de que Nvidia contratara a otro ejecutivo de Apple: el exCEO Tim Cook. Matt Garman, director de Servicios Web de Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ), es otro ejecutivo que, al igual que Huang, combina experiencia técnica y operativa. Dirige un extenso negocio que alquila capacidad de procesamiento informático de una vasta red de centros de datos, incluidos los chips propios de Amazon. Una crítica que se le hace es que Amazon inicialmente se consideró rezagada con respecto a competidores como Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ) o Google en el desarrollo de infraestructura de IA. Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO de Micron Technology Inc. ( MU ), sabe lo que significa dirigir una empresa de chips durante los ciclos de auge y caída. Ha liderado un aumento de más del 2700% en las acciones de la compañía, impulsado por el alza de los precios de la memoria debido a la demanda generada por la IA. Ver más: ¿Y ahora qué hago con mis acciones de Nvidia? Las claves para decidir tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang Sin embargo, su experiencia se centra principalmente en la memoria y la fabricación, más que en la arquitectura de unidades de procesamiento gráfico y el ecosistema de software. Amin Vahdat, de Google, supervisa el programa de unidades de procesamiento tensorial de la compañía, otro rival por el dominio de Nvidia en el mercado de chips de IA. Sus credenciales técnicas son formidables, pero al igual que varios candidatos con un fuerte perfil de ingeniería en la lista, tiene menos experiencia dirigiendo una empresa pública de gran envergadura con la magnitud, la complejidad comercial y el escrutinio de los inversores de Nvidia. Ver más: Cuánto dinero perdió Jensen Huang de su fortuna antes de renunciar como CEO de Nvidia Tres miembros de la familia de Huang trabajan en Nvidia: sus hijos Spencer y Madison, así como su yerno Nico Caprez. Como vicepresidente de crecimiento de infraestructura global de IA, Caprez ocupa el puesto más destacado de los tres y es conocido por su gran participación en conversaciones con proveedores de computación en la nube para IA y otras operaciones de centros de datos. Huang ha declarado que no desea que sus hijos asuman la responsabilidad de dirigir Nvidia y que “tendrán que ganársela”. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

ANTALYA: World leaders have set out competing positions and made clashing demands in two days of intense speech-making at the COP31 climate change talks in Türkiye , leaving negotiators with a tough task to draft a meaningful deal that all can agree.
Small island states, among the most vulnerable in the world as global warming makes sea levels rise, pleaded for urgent cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.
European leaders , meanwhile, lined up behind a proposal to expand global electrification, developing countries asked for more finance from rich ones, and fossil fuel producers said oil, gas, and coal should continue to be used.
"We reaffirm our sovereign right to strengthen our energy and oil industry as a driver of our national development," Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez told the conference, after UN leaders had made the case for bringing to an end the age of fossil fuel.

Apart from trying to accommodate incompatible national positions aired on Wednesday (Nov 11) and Thursday (Nov 12), conference host Türkiye and negotiations lead Australia also have the challenge of trying to make progress when wars and inflation have pushed climate concerns down the political agenda.
"It's my job to steer consensus, not to bang tables and demand any particular action, but to steer consensus to the strongest , most ambitious possible out come within the constraints of that consensus-driven process," Chris Bowen, Australia's COP31 president of negotiations , told Reuters.
Asked what a good deal might look like, he said: "I have many more hours of consultations with partners to do."
Climate activists say short-term political concerns should not get in the way of addressing an issue that will get more pressing if ignored.
A UN report last month found the world was already on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.
"The situation could not be less under control. The planet is not dying. It is being killed," Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg said on the sidelines of the UN conference.
"It is being killed by the very same people often thought to come to our rescue. No one is coming to our rescue."

BRITAIN'S BURNHAM BACKS RENEWABLES Earlier on Thursday, the leaders of small island states including the Bahamas, Tuvalu, the Solomon Islands and Saint Lucia called for swift action.
"Major emitters must move beyond the usual promises. They must reduce emissions that the climate crisis demands," said Saint Lucia's Prime Minister Philip J . Pierre.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham backed a proposal by Turkey to increase electricity's share of world energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035, from a little over a fifth now, to help advance that goal. Turkey has not specified whether the extra energy used would be renewable.
Burnham told the conference that energy supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war with Ukraine showed clean energy was the wise choice.
"It is now plain for everyone to see that if we depend on energy we do not control, then we leave ourselves exposed to prices we cannot control," he said. "The shift to clean energy is the only r out e to energy security."
Developing countries reiterated requests that they have made during many years of UN talks for rich countries to provide more finance to help them shift to cleaner energy, adapt to a warming world , and repair climate-driven destruction.
Fernanda de Carvalho, the head of climate policy for the World Wildlife Fund environmental group, said he found the leaders ' speeches underwhelming, especially as COP31 i s the first UN conference since scientists have publicly said the world is set to breach the 1.5C threshold.
"It is worrying that the climate issue is not as high on the global political agenda as it needs to be," he said.

items.title: Investors worry the AI trade might lose Nvidia’s largesse after Huang
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: As chip giant Nvidia’s chief Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday, investors’ biggest fears were as much about the future of the multitrillion-dollar company as its ability and willingness to ...
items.body: SINGAPORE -- As chip giant Nvidia’s chief Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday, investors’ biggest fears were as much about the future of the multitrillion-dollar company as its ability and willingness to continue bankrolling the AI boom. Huang’s exit is yet another pressure point on the global markets’ most crowded trade and came after the board of the world’s dominant chipmaker, at the cutting edge of computing, met late on Wednesday to decide the longtime CEO’s fate after reports of his two extramarital affairs. The company said Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor. Traders’ first reaction was to punish Nvidia shares and those of its customers, including data-centre firms CoreWeave and Naver, while pushing shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and AMD higher. Shares in China’s leading makers of graphics processing units (GPUs) surged, as the leadership upheaval at Nvidia boosted expectations that local chip suppliers could win greater market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon all jumped nearly 10 per cent. Nvidia shares pared premarket losses but were still down nearly five per cent at 1600 GMT. The worry in the market is that the stakes are far higher and that if Nvidia — under a different leader — backs away from a strategy of financing data centers, then the AI boom itself loses momentum. “Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI.’ They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. Nvidia has been the banner stock of the AI revolution, with its chip technology ahead of rivals and enormous sales driving the share price up some 900 per cent over the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT ushered in the AI era. But Nvidia has also become a torchbearer and financier, anticipating demand for ever more powerful chips while sinking billions of dollars into funding its own customers via a mix of equity investments and other promises. “Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.” Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang following reports he had an extramarital affair with a businesswoman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy. A subsequent report about another affair came out ahead of Wednesday’s board meeting. Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, said Nvidia’s revenue would not suddenly plunge after Huang’s exit and, therefore, the bigger concern was about the future, given Huang was the person with the vision for computing. “Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” he said. Nvidia sinks and takes some, but not all, along Huang’s departure leaves a vacuum at the top of the roughly US$4 trillion chipmaker that he co-founded and built over more than three decades to become the top supplier of chips and the nexus of the U.S.-China technology rivalry. Chipmakers in Asia, whose stocks have soared with Nvidia and the AI spending boom, but lately sagged on worries about funding costs and the demand outlook, slipped. Nvidia listed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its most recent earnings report, with an obligation capped at $105 billion on an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and lease and other capacity guarantees topping $50 billion. In August, it said it had partnered with six major financial institutions including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone to launch compute financing platforms aimed at raising over $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said then the company had the option to backstop up to $125 billion, or 25 per cent of the potential deals. “The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility,” said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers in Connecticut. Nvidia is also one of the investors in Claude chatbot creator Anthropic’s initial public offering. The listing this month is set to serve as a test of investor appetite for all things AI. Shares in Nvidia-backed data-centre operator CoreWeave, which surged on Wednesday on upbeat earnings, fell more than six per cent. Shares in South Korea’s Naver, in which Nvidia took a $1 billion stake by financing a data-center expansion, also dropped six per cent. To be sure, investors said, the quality of Nvidia’s products is not likely to change, and change at the top won’t quickly hit demand. “Nvidia’s core asset is its advanced GPUs, which still have no real substitute in the market,” said Anna Wu, founder of Floodlines Research. “The AI trade rests on that demand, not on one individual.” But when the company reports earnings next week, the focus will inevitably be on leadership, strategy and whether a sales outlook formed under Huang still holds up under a successor. (Reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore, Tom Westbrook in Sydney, Prathik Jayaprakash, Anhata Rooprai, Lakshmi Tharuniyaa, Johann Cherian in Bengaluru and Li Gu in Shanghai; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus, Vidya Ranganathan, Mark Potter and Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid deepening scandal, leaving AI chip giant at crossroads

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO. Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, will not remain on the board.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (Nov 12) after revelations of two extramarital affairs , including one involving a suspected Chinese spy , plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.
Huang's exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia , one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO's push to preserve access to the Chinese market, as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump.
The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration's oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment.
Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lutnick's future. Earlier in the day, a White House official said US President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position."
Huang's departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia 's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly US$6 trillion.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Related:

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago.
Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang's departure.
Nvidia shares were down about 4.8 per cent, paring earlier losses. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6 per cent each.
Huang, Nvidia 's fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61 per cent stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair.
"The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18.
Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving.
Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said.
The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation.
REPLACING HUANG Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.
While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia 's reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products.
"The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.
"In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself."
Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

TRUMP WEIGHS IN Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.
Trump had urged Huang to fight for his job in a call on Tuesday, the New York Times reported.
On Thursday, the US president suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia 's CEO.
US House Speaker Mike Johnson said it was "critically important for right successor to be chosen to replace Huang", noting there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China.
HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company.
That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies.
The scandal preceding Huang's departure unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips.
Subsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.
Washington has also investigated Megaspeed over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports.

Separately, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that the US Justice Department was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China, citing a person familiar with the matter.
A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney’s office declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The office previously charged three people associated with Super Micro, including its co-founder, with helping smuggle at least US$2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Earlier, the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs said Singapore police had been investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe into Megaspeed and Alice Huang. The police had reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for help and had received "limited information or assistance," the ministry said.
Earlier this month, Nvidia 's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.
The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia 's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

Huang's exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia , one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO's push to preserve access to the Chinese market, as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump.
The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration's oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment.
Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly US$6 trillion.

"The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18.
Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving.
Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said.
The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation.

The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.

"The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.

NEW YORK: The death toll from a residential building collapse in New York rose to at least eight, including two children, on Thursday (Nov 12), after more bodies were recovered from the rubble, officials said.

Rescuers worked through the night, searching the site in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn where the three-story building collapsed on Wednesday.

They recovered four more bodies overnight, while two others died in the hospital, Fire Chief Lillian Bonsignore told a news conference.

That brought the death toll to eight, including two children, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, adding that another 19 people were injured and one is in critical condition.

"This has been a devastating morning and evening for our city," he said.

Shop worker James Williams, 60, said he witnessed the building collapse after hearing loud banging noises throughout the morning.

"I smelled the smoke from the fumes, and I was watching bricks fall. But to see, like two minutes later, to see the building collapse and fall, it was just devastating," he told AFP.

"There were people trying to get out ... I saw somebody on the side of the staircase, and I'll be honest with you, I didn't even really want to think about that."

Members of the New York City Fire Department and first responders search for victims in the rubble a day after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on Nov 12, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Charly Triballeau)

Another witness, 14-year-old Kenneilia Reid, told AFP: "When I was walking by, I started seeing dust all of a sudden, and I was like, what is going on? When I turned my back, I saw the whole building collapse." 

The building, a three-story structure dating from 1930 with four apartments and a commercial space on the ground floor, collapsed onto a nearby excavation site.

A massive emergency response was launched, with about 250 firefighters and rescue workers and search dogs on site. 

An adjacent building was also affected, with one of its walls torn away, leaving a staircase and rooms exposed on the rubble.

The cause of the collapse was not immediately clear, and firefighters continued to work at the site on Thursday.
STOP-WORK ORDER "My stomach hurts. I can't imagine you were just in your kitchen doing something" and then "you're not any place. It's crazy," Annemarie, a 60-year-old care worker who did not want to share her last name, told AFP. She lives on the street behind the collapsed building.

"It could have been me, you know, it's really scary," she said.

The building fell into an adjacent work site, where construction workers had been excavating, Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of New York's Department of Buildings, told a press conference late Wednesday.

Tigani said that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building.

Members of the New York City Fire Department and first responders search for victims in the rubble a day after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on Nov 12, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Charly Triballeau)

According to documents from the city's building department reviewed by AFP, the construction site had been issued a stop-work order in April due to potentially dangerous demolition conditions. 

However, work continued, resulting in a US$10,000 fine for the company involved. No link has yet been established between these violations and the building's collapse.

Mamdani said five main entities were involved at the site and authorities on Thursday started "sweeping" 100 other construction sites they are associated with around the city.

The mayor promised a thorough investigation and to hold anyone responsible "fully accountable." 

The city's Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene "assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings."

Source: Reuters/as

As the centrepiece of the AI ecosystem, Nvidia finances infrastructure built around its chips - a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens.

FAST

Global AI-linked stocks tumbled on Thursday as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a deepening scandal around his affairs, upending the chipmaker's leadership and posing fresh risks to a sector already reeling with funding and regulatory concerns.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said.
As the centrepiece of the AI ecosystem, the chipmaker finances infrastructure built around its chips - a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens.
Nvidia's shares fell 8.2 per cent to a more than 16-month low in early trading and its market value was on track to close below US$4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.

"Nvidia has been called the 'Bank of AI'. If they have to take a step back because of what's going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That's an open question," said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading.
Nvidia-backed neocloud firm CoreWeave dropped 9.1 per cent after surging more than 27 per cent in the previous session when its earnings ignited a relief rally in AI stocks.
Other neocloud stocks, including IREN and Applied Digital, were also trading lower. Nebius dropped 16.2 per cent after the company said its 2026 revenue would come in at the low end of its previous forecast.
Nvidia has lost more than US$550 billion in market value since the board announced an investigation on Sunday into Huang's relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy.
"The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility. We're going to find out over the next few weeks as this whole situation unravels," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.
Nvidia short sellers have made US$9.6 billion in on-paper profits so far this week, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.

Related:

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid deepening scandal, leaving AI chip giant at crossroads

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

Nvidia, CEO Jensen Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy

AI SELLOFF CONTINUES AFTER BRIEF RESPITE Chipmakers, widely viewed as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, led the selloff with the Philadelphia chips index sliding 1.3 per cent.
Marvell Technology, which Huang called the "next trillion-dollar company" in June, slumped 3.8 per cent. AI hyperscaler Oracle, which is expanding its cloud AI chip deals with Nvidia, shed 2.6 per cent.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology fell 2.5 per cent and data storage firms Sandisk and Western Digital eased 6 per cent and 3.7 per cent. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent and AI server maker Dell eased between 3 per cent and 5.1 per cent.
Construction and power-generation equipment maker Caterpillar and power producer Vistra slipped about 0.5 per cent each.
Shares of AMD and Broadcom, which also produce AI chips and compete with Nvidia, however, rose 3.7 per cent and 5.6 per cent, respectively, on expectations that the turmoil at Nvidia could create opportunity for rivals.
Other hyperscalers including Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft were also up between 0.8 per cent and 2.7 per cent.
AI stocks struggled and the Nasdaq entered a technical correction earlier this month after the Democrats swept the midterm elections, including in states opposed to data centres, stoking fears tighter regulation could slow the AI build-out.
Tech-heavy stock markets across the globe witnessed jitters. Japan and South Korea closed nearly 0.7 per cent lower. Tech stocks in Europe were also down about 1 per cent.
Nvidia trades at about 12 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since November 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Source: Reuters/rk

items.title: WRAPUP 2-US labor market resilient; existing home sales hit more than 16-year low in October
items.summary: Read more about WRAPUP 2-US labor market resilient; existing home sales hit more than 16-year low in October on Devdiscourse ...
items.body:
WRAPUP 2-US labor market resilient; existing home sales hit more than 16-year low in October
Reuters | Updated: 12-11-2026 23:19 IST | Created: 12-11-2026 23:19 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits increased more than expected last week, but remained at a level consistent with a stable labor market, allowing the Federal Reserve to focus on fighting inflation. Economists expect layoffs to remain low through the end of the year, though seasonal volatility related to the holiday season could cause some spikes in the claims data. The government last week reported a surge in nonfarm payrolls in October and a decline in the unemployment rate to 4.1% from 4.2% in September. The resilience in the labor market is despite the ongoing Middle East conflict, which is boosting inflation.
"Firms are continuing to hold on to labor," said Olivia Cross, senior US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. "We expect layoffs to remain low through the fourth quarter, but then come under some pressure next year in response to the recent tightening of financial conditions and the growing use of AI by firms." Initial claims for state unemployment benefits rose 9,000 to a seasonally adjusted 200,000 for the week ended November 7, the Labor Department said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 195,000 claims for the latest week.
Claims have stayed at or below 200,000 since mid-September and remain close to the 189,000 level touched in mid-July, the lowest since 1969, raising the prospect that the labor market could be tightening. But with wages growing at a moderate pace, most economists do not believe that is the case. Some argue that a smaller workforce, due to retirements and the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, is the key driver of the historically low level of claims.
"A generally smaller labor force could mean fewer workers to file for unemployment insurance," said Veronica Clark, an economist at Citigroup. "Of course, this would still be consistent with a low unemployment rate, with continuing claims suggesting the unemployment rate may even fall further towards around 4.0% in data by early 2027." The claims report showed that the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, fell 20,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.697 million during the week ended October 31. But the so-called continuing claims do not include some unemployed people, such as recent college graduates and others who have little or no work history.
Some people might also have exhausted their eligibility for benefits, limited to 26 weeks in most states, keeping continuing claims at relatively low levels. The median duration of unemployment jumped to 11.9 weeks in October, the longest since November 2021, from 11.5 weeks in September. Though businesses have been hoarding workers, they have remained reluctant to increase headcount, with economists citing uncertainty from the US-Israeli war with Iran, now in its ninth month. Businesses were also unsure of their staffing needs as they embraced AI.
US central bank Governor Michael Barr warned on Thursday the nation should be prepared for "serious short-term disruptions" to the job market because of AI, which he said, depending on how fast it is deployed, could begin displacing workers at scale and widening inequality in favor of investors. Stocks on Wall Street were trading lower as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit and rising oil prices following comments by President Donald Trump that the US did not need a deal with Iran weighed on sentiment. The dollar advanced against a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields rose.
HOUSE PRICES STILL ELEVATED Government data this week showed consumer prices increasing faster than expected in October. That, together with comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller, prompted financial markets to almost fully price in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, and to anticipate another increase in January.
The Fed left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. While the labor market continues to hold up, rising mortgage rates stemming from the Iran war are depressing the interest-rate-sensitive housing market. Sales of previously owned homes tumbled 5.5% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units, the National Association of Realtors said in a separate report. That was the lowest level since August 2010, when sales were declining as a homebuyers tax credit ended. The incentive was aimed at stimulating demand following the 2008 global financial crisis.
Economists had forecast home resales falling to a rate of 3.85 million units. Sales plunged 8.8% on a year-over-year basis in October. The drop in sales was across all price categories, including those priced $1 million and above, which had experienced strong growth in prior months. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate jumped above 7% in late August, rising to 7.40% by mid-September, for a total of 142 basis points since the US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February, data from mortgage finance agency Freddie Mac showed.
It averaged 7.11% in the latest week, down from 7.18% in the prior week. "Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023," said Lawrence Yun, the NAR's chief economist.
The NAR's Housing Affordability Index dropped to 100.7 from 107.3 in October 2025. Existing housing inventory increased 1.3% to 1.590 million units, the highest level since November 2019. Supply rose 4.6% from a year ago. At October's sales pace, it would take 5.1 months to exhaust the current inventory of existing homes, the most since November 2015. That was up from 4.4 months a year ago. The median existing home price last month advanced 0.4% from a year ago to $421,900, the highest for any October.
First-time buyers accounted for 29% of sales, down from 32% a year ago. A 40% share in this category is needed for a robust housing market. The housing market weakness is demand-related, with higher prices keeping distressed sales at a negligible 2%. "With mortgage rates expected to remain above 7% through most of 2027, we expect home sales to remain below 4 million until late next year," said Nancy Vanden Houten, lead US economist at Oxford Economics.

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

REG - KR1 PLC - Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations Refinitiv 3 min read

KR1
RNS Number : 7982C KR1 PLC 12 November 2026   KR1 plc
Thursday, 12 November 2026
KR1 plc (“KR1” or the “Company”)
Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations
KR1 plc KR1 , a London Stock Exchange-listed onchain infrastructure company, is pleased to provide an update on its Venice (“VVV”) operations.
Following its October Infrastructure Income & Holdings update, in which it reported holding 276,223 VVV valued at £5.77 million as at 30 September 2026, the Company has fully staked its current holding of 275,000 VVV, earning rewards in VVV at an indicative annualised staking rate of approximately 5.74% as at 11 November 2026. Based on available disclosures, the Company believes it is the largest publicly listed holder of VVV, with approximately 0.56% of the circulating supply, a position that reflects its conviction in the convergence of AI and crypto.
Venice is a core holding within KR1’s Technology Infrastructure Strategy. In its Introducing Decentralised AI announcement on 14 May 2026, the Company disclosed an initial holding of 60,000 VVV and the commencement of staking operations. KR1 has since increased its position. Founded by renowned crypto entrepreneur Erik Voorhees, Venice provides access to frontier and open-source AI models for generating text, code, images, video and audio. The platform is designed around privacy, model choice and user control.
Venice’s adoption continues to accelerate. Its October community update reported 5 million users, with the increase from 4 million taking 68 days. Daily inference volume exceeded one trillion tokens during October, compared with approximately 250 billion at the end of September.
On 14 October, Venice’s Erik Voorhees reported annual revenue exceeding US$150 million. In July, Venice also announced a US$65 million Series A led by Dragonfly, at a stated US$1 billion valuation, to expand its consumer platform and API business.
KR1 puts its Venice assets to productive use in two ways. First, the Company stakes VVV to generate infrastructure income in the form of newly issued VVV tokens. Reward rates vary, and standard VVV unstaking is subject to a seven-day cooldown. The second route uses DIEM, a token that holders can mint by locking staked VVV. KR1 acquired its DIEM separately and stakes it to access daily credits for AI inference on Venice. KR1 makes that inference capacity available to customers through third-party marketplaces.
Venice’s buy-and-burn programme creates a further connection between commercial adoption and VVV. The platform allocates 5% of API credit purchases to buying VVV on the open market and permanently removing it from supply. New Pro, Pro+ and Max subscriptions trigger purchases and burns of US$2, US$5 and US$10, respectively, alongside discretionary burns.
Venice reported that the value of VVV burned during October had exceeded US$1 million by 28 October. Revenue-funded purchases create demand for VVV, while burns reduce VVV supply relative to continuing issuance. This mechanism is separate from staking rewards and does not constitute a cash distribution to token holders.
Keld van Schreven, Managing Director and Co-Founder of KR1 plc, commented:
“We believe the convergence of AI and crypto could be one of the defining technology themes of the next decade. We put that conviction to work through our Venice operations, staking VVV to earn infrastructure income while retaining exposure to the platform’s growth. We can use those rewards to fund operations or reinvest them in productive assets. That reinvestment drives the KR1 flywheel, helping grow the earning capacity behind each KR1 equity share.”

KR1 plc owns and operates productive digital assets across the networks powering the convergence of AI and crypto. As the only dedicated onchain infrastructure company listed on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, KR1 draws on a decade of domain expertise to take a high-conviction, thesis-driven approach to its holdings, targeting a dual return profile: infrastructure income and capital appreciation.

items.title: Blast at steel plant kills 16 in Turkey
items.author: Marina Meireles
items.creator: Marina Meireles
items.summary: Another 13 people were injured following the blast, and 10 others are still waiting to be rescued.
items.body:
Blast at steel plant kills 16 in Turkey

Marina Meireles | November 9, 2026 | 1:01 pm
News   Europe   Iron Ore  

Stock image.

A blast at a steel and iron plant in western Turkey killed 16 people on Nov. 9, with search and rescue operations still ongoing to reach 10 people still trapped under the rubble, President Tayyip Erdogan said.

The explosion happened around noon local time, at the Habas Demir Celik facility in the Aliaga district of Turkey’s Izmir province, where iron and steel are processed.

The incident occured when a ceiling crane snapped and fell into an arc furnace during the molten steel casting process. 

13 people were injured, and 2 were in serious condition, Bloomberg reported. The victims were transported to different hospitals in the region. 

The government said the incident is under investigation.

(With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)

items.title: Copper price bounces after worst week since March amid scramble for metal in China
items.author: Frik Els
items.creator: Frik Els
items.summary: The Yangshan premium for copper shipped into China climbed to a record $230 a tonne on Monday, spot premiums in Shanghai have tripled in two weeks, and deliverable stocks on the SHFE would cover less than a day of Chinese consumption.
items.body:
Copper price bounces after worst week since March amid scramble for metal in China

Staff Writer | November 9, 2026 | 12:39 pm
Markets   China   United States   Copper  

Copper cathode production in electrowinning plant. ( Stock image by Jorge. )

Copper prices rebounded on Monday, recovering part of last week’s steep losses as risk appetite steadied, the dollar slipped and tight physical supply in China came back into focus.

Comex copper for December delivery, the most active contract in New York, was trading at $6.3550 a pound ($14,010 a tonne) late morning in New York, up 1.9% on the day and roughly 13% higher so far in 2026.

On the London Metal Exchange, three-month copper rose 0.9% to $13,890 a tonne by mid-afternoon in London, having lost 2.7% last week in its steepest weekly decline since March. In Shanghai the most-traded contract gained 0.5% to 107,430 yuan ($16,096) a tonne.

China squeeze

“Copper is recovering as risk sentiment stabilises and tight physical supply in China returns to focus,” ING commodities strategist Ewa Manthey told Reuters, adding that the rise in spot premiums shows metal remains difficult to secure.

The Yangshan copper premium, which reflects demand for metal imported into the top consumer, rose to a record $230 a tonne on Monday. Copper stocks in Shanghai Futures Exchange-monitored warehouses fell more than 24% last week to 33,848 tonnes, the lowest in almost three years, according to John Gross of The Copper Journal . That would cover China’s copper consumption for less than a day.

Bloomberg reports the Singapore-based trader Trafigura, one of the biggest in the copper market, has over the past two weeks approached several producers and traders in Asia seeking to buy large volumes over November and December, and has been willing to outbid rivals to secure cargoes.

Spot premiums in Shanghai have tripled over the past two weeks to a record 2,615 yuan ($392) a tonne, according to Shanghai Metals Market, while premiums for imported copper tracked by Fastmarkets have jumped more than 40% to $195–210 a tonne, the highest in data going back to 2017. On the SHFE, the spread between December and January contracts blew out to more than 1,200 yuan a tonne late on Friday, the widest backwardation since 2005.

Chinese smelters are struggling to source concentrate and scrap, and a crackdown on illegal mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo – China’s biggest source of refined copper – in which the government seized more than 500 trucks and several thousand tonnes of copper and cobalt, threatens to crimp supplies further.

“One of the main drivers for the tightness is the slowdown in refined production growth, which reflects the fact that smelters have been struggling for feedstock,” Morgan Stanley metals strategist Amy Gower told Bloomberg. “The demand indicators are fairly lackluster, so it does point to supply issues being the cause of the tightness in the Chinese market.”

Ship to shore

Comex depots hold 732,943 tonnes, more than double a year ago, after two years in which miners and traders prioritised shipments to the US ahead of threatened import tariffs.

On paper, the surge in Shanghai premiums and spreads is now large enough to cover the cost of shipping copper from the US back to China. The hindrance, people familiar with the trade told Bloomberg, is that those cargoes would be worth far more in the US if tariffs are eventually imposed.

“This is starting to become more of a question, but for it to happen I think you’d need tariffs to be definitively ruled out,” Gower said. “Our base case is that the US material will be quite sticky and will only get drawn down through under-importing.”

Temporary gains?

Monday’s bounce may not hold. “Today’s move does not necessarily mark the end of the correction,” ING’s Manthey said. “Prices remain vulnerable to further weakness if broader market sentiment deteriorates again.”

A Democratic sweep in last week’s US midterm elections has reduced the prospects for the Trump administration’s planned tariffs on refined copper and raised the odds of tighter restrictions on data centres, threatening both the AI-related demand and the tariff-driven stockpiling that have supported prices this year. TD Securities said on Friday that copper faces a further slide as the result weakens expectations for import tariffs.

Last week also offered a partial answer to the question of how much of copper’s 2026 rally rests on AI hype rather than fundamentals. Gross says: the metal fell in lockstep with tech stocks. The physical demand story has not changed – US construction spending on data centres hit a record annualized $96.5 billion in September, according to The Copper Journal – but a “not in my backyard” contingent emboldened by the election could see that spending stall too.

Citi struck a similar note on Monday: “While low visible inventories and elevated geopolitical risks should continue to provide downside support in the near-term, the outlook for next year remains challenged by Indonesian-led supply growth and a muted demand environment.”

Miners rebound

Copper producers rallied with the metal on Monday. Freeport-McMoRan climbed 5.8% in early afternoon trade in New York, lifting its market value to $90.2 billion, less than a week after its board approved a $4.5 billion expansion of the Bagdad mine in Arizona that would more than double the operation’s copper output to over 400 million pounds a year from mid-2030 and make it the second-largest copper mine in the US.

Southern Copper added 6.0% to $151.3 billion and Teck Resources rose 5.9% to $31.4 billion. BHP gained 3.2% to $207.4 billion, Rio Tinto 3.0% to $147.8 billion and Glencore 5.3% to $81.7 billion. Anglo American was up 6.2% and Antofagasta 6.7% in US trading, with Lundin Mining up 6.5% and First Quantum Minerals 5.2% in Toronto.

Ivanhoe Mines added 3.5%, but the Vancouver-based company is still down 47% this year after a second production downgrade at its Kamoa-Kakula complex in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The bounce follows a brutal October. The MINING.COM TOP 50 ranking of the world’s most valuable miners lost $226 billion last month on top of September’s $264 billion decline, and is now $712 billion below its February peak.

In project news, Rio Tinto is injecting $144 million into Resolution Copper in Arizona after a land-swap court victory, a project JPMorgan says is central to its view that US copper output could more than double . In Chile, Codelco and Pucobre have cleared a key hurdle for an $870 million copper mine slated to begin construction in 2027, even as the state miner contends with an inflated output scandal that has grown to 42,100 tonnes.

items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国のテンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は、東南アジアでオラクルから先端のAI半導体を借り受けることで合意した。テンセントにとってAI半導体のリース契約としては過去最大規模となる。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）が事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。

報道によると、テンセントは、5年間の契約の一環として10万個の半導体を利用できるようになる。契約額は70億ドル（約1兆1000億円）に上るという。

中国のAI開発企業は米国の輸出規制を回避するため、米エヌビディア製など中国国内では入手できないAIアクセラレーターを海外で借りて利用している。中国のテクノロジー企業は、東南アジアのデータセンターの最大顧客層の一つとなっている。

テンセントとオラクルの担当者は、ブルームバーグ・ニュースのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。
